articles.title: MLS round-up: Inter Miami win without Messi as Griezmann and Lewandowski make debuts
articles.summary: Catch up with the latest action from Major League Soccer.
articles.content:
MLS round-up: Inter Miami win without Messi as Griezmann and Lewandowski make debuts

Catch up with the latest action from Major League Soccer.

Last Update:

Major League Soccer returned from its six-week World Cup break on Wednesday night with a statement of intent from the competition’s biggest names, and it was a 39-year-old Uruguayan, not the two marquee European arrivals making their debuts, who stole the show.

Table of Contents

Miami march on without Messi

Inter Miami handled business at Nu Stadium, beating Chicago Fire 3-2 in a pulsating return to action.

With Lionel Messi and Rodrigo De Paul taking extended rest following Argentina’s run to the World Cup final, it fell to Luis Suarez to keep Miami’s momentum alive.

The veteran Uruguayan delivered, scoring twice to send the Herons to a fifth consecutive victory and take his tally for the season to eight goals.

Chicago opened the scoring through an own goal in the 18th minute before Suarez stepped up from the spot in the 28th to level, converting coolly after David Ruiz was fouled inside the box by Jack Elliott.

German Berterame put Miami ahead before the break, but Puso Dithejane came off the bench to equalise in the 67th minute with a first-touch finish from inside the area.

It looked as though the points might be shared until homegrown midfielder Preston Plambeck arrived in the 87th minute to score his first-ever MLS goal and send Nu Stadium into raptures.

Miami are now five points behind Nashville SC in the Supporters’ Shield race, with a Matchday 18 trip to CF Montreal coming up on Saturday.

Lewandowski’s debut falls flat

It was an eventful night for Chicago despite the defeat, with legendary Polish striker Robert Lewandowski making his long-awaited MLS debut as a starter at Nu Stadium.

Having arrived in the United States only a little over a week ago, the 37-year-old came off the bench at half-time and offered glimpses of his quality without being able to change the outcome.

Head coach Gregg Berhalter was measured in his assessment of what to expect from Lewandowski in the weeks ahead, tempering expectations while making clear the impact will come.

“It was a priority for us to get him on the field today,” Berhalter said. “He’s only trained for seven or eight days, so we expect him to make a big impact as he continues to get fit.

“Like any player, you build up, you get strong, you get your power, and then you’re good. The timing is different for every player. We’re not in preseason right now, we’re in the middle of a season, and that’s something to consider.”

Griezmann off the mark immediately

It is hard to imagine Antoine Griezmann’s Orlando City debut going any better than it did on Wednesday night in California.

The 35-year-old Frenchman, signed from Atletico Madrid in March and the club’s all-time leading scorer with 211 goals in 488 appearances across his two spells in the Spanish capital, announced himself to the Orlando faithful as the Lions hammered San Jose Earthquakes 4-0 at PayPal Park.

Eduard Atuesta was the creative force behind the performance with three assists, but it was Griezmann who provided the moment the crowd had been waiting for.

David Brekalo opened the scoring in the seventh minute with an unmarked header from Atuesta’s perfectly placed free kick. Ivan Angulo made it 2-0 in the 29th minute, ripping a low shot past Angus Gunn with no pressure to speak of. Then, 48 minutes in, Griezmann got his moment.

Justin Ellis picked off a pass in the attacking third and found the Frenchman, who slipped past a trio of defenders before firing a low shot inside the near post.

Griezmann led the game in chances created with five, led Orlando for touches and passes, and stayed on for the full 90 minutes.

The result lifts Orlando to 10th in the Eastern Conference, just two points behind DC United for the final play-off position.

articles.title: Inter Miami hit with investigation into Casemiro signing
articles.summary: Inter Miami are being investigated after signing Casemiro ahead of LA Galaxy this summer.
articles.content:
Inter Miami hit with investigation into Casemiro signing

Inter Miami are being investigated after signing Casemiro ahead of LA Galaxy this summer.

Last Update:

Major League Soccer has launched an investigation into alleged tampering by Inter Miami following the club’s signing of Brazil midfielder Casemiro.

Inter Miami confirmed on Wednesday that the 34-year-old had joined the club after leaving Manchester United at the end of last season, signing a contract through to the end of the 2027 MLS campaign with the option of a further extension until June 2029.

Shortly after the announcement, MLS revealed it was reviewing a potential breach of its rules.

“The league is gathering all relevant information and will refrain from further comment until the review is complete,” the league said in a statement.

“While Inter Miami CF and the LA Galaxy have reached a settlement for the discovery priority to sign Casemiro, the terms will be released upon conclusion of the tampering investigation.”

The investigation centres on MLS discovery rights, which give one club first refusal should a listed player wish to join the league. Each MLS club can hold discovery rights for up to five players at any one time.

LA Galaxy held Casemiro’s discovery rights before Inter Miami announced they had acquired them as part of the deal.

The Galaxy confirmed an agreement had been reached but said details would remain confidential until the league’s investigation is complete.

Casemiro waves goodbye to Manchester United

Casemiro announced in January that he would leave Manchester United by mutual consent following the expiry of his contract at the end of the 2026-27 season.

The midfielder enjoyed a trophy-laden spell at Real Madrid before joining United in 2022, winning five Champions League titles in Spain.

He made 160 appearances for the Red Devils, scoring 26 goals and providing 14 assists while lifting the FA Cup and EFL Cup.

He also featured for Brazil as they reached the last-16 of this summer’s World Cup.

“What motivates me the most, and I think this is true for every player, is winning and continuing to grow,” Casemiro said following his move.

United have already moved to strengthen their midfield after his departure, signing Andrey Santos from Chelsea and Youri Tielemans from Aston Villa during the summer transfer window.

Inter Miami co-owner David Beckham welcomed the arrival of the experienced midfielder.

“He is a winner who has achieved so much in the game and after such an incredible career with Real Madrid and Manchester United, I’m delighted that he’s decided to make Miami his next home,” Beckham said.

At Inter Miami, Casemiro joins former Real Madrid and Manchester United team-mate Sergio Reguilon, as well as Argentina internationals Lionel Messi and Rodrigo De Paul.

It is not the first time Inter Miami have faced scrutiny over their transfer dealings.

In 2021, the club was fined $2 million after breaching MLS roster regulations relating to the signing of Blaise Matuidi from Juventus.

The league found the France midfielder’s compensation exceeded the permitted limits, effectively giving Miami four designated players instead of the maximum three allowed under MLS rules.

The designated player rule, commonly known as the “Beckham Rule”, was introduced following Beckham’s move to LA Galaxy in 2007.

articles.title: Saliba out for ‘extended period’ after back injury for France at World Cup
articles.summary: Saliba went off in the 30th minute of France's World Cup defeat to Spain
articles.content:
Saliba out for ‘extended period’ after back injury for France at World Cup

Saliba went off in the 30th minute of France's World Cup defeat to Spain

Last Update:

Arsenal say defender William Saliba will be out for an “extended period” after a back injury at the World Cup for France.

The centre-back will not require surgery on an injury which saw him substituted in the 30th minute of France’s semi-final defeat tp Spain, but is likely to miss a significant part of Arsenal’s Premier League title defence.

Saliba was one of the standout performers in the Gunners’ title-winning campaign last season, making 50 appearances in all competitions.

Arsenal kick off their 2026-27 campaign against Manchester City in the Community Shield on Sunday, August 16, before the Gunners begin the Premier League season against Coventry five days later.

An Arsenal statement said: “William Saliba has returned to us from World Cup duty, where he played an integral role in France reaching the semi-finals of the competition.

“Subsequent specialist reviews on William’s return to London this week have confirmed that he has suffered a back injury which will require a period of rehabilitation.

“Extensive assessments have concluded that surgery is not recommended, but William should now commence a managed recovery programme.

“William’s rehabilitation will commence immediately, with continual management of his injury, and he is expected to be out of action for an extended period.

“Everyone is fully focused on supporting William to ensure he is back to full fitness as soon as possible.”

Saliba injury: Do Arsenal need a new centre-back?

Arsenal already knew they would be without their main centre-back for a period, but news of the length of that absence will almost certainly see them step up their search for a new defender.

Ezri Konsa and unattached John Stones have both been mentioned as potential targets, with a bid of £30million reportedly rejected by Aston Villa for the former.

Villa are likely to demand much more for the England international, which could make Stones a more viable option, albeit questions remain over the former Manchester City man’s fitness.

The 32-year-old played five times for the Three Lions at the World Cup, including every minute of the quarter-final and semi-final, but he started only five times for City in the Premier League last term.

Revealed: Five attackers Arsenal could target after missing out on Morgan Rogers

Arsenal are in need of a new left-sided forward after being snubbed by Rogers

After weeks and even months linking Arsenal with Morgan Rogers, the England forward will be lining up in the blue of Chelsea next season in what is a huge blow for the Premier League champions.

articles.summary: Casemiro left Manchester United after four years this summer
articles.content:
Casemiro’s next club revealed after leaving Manchester United – but league opens investigation into tampering claims

Casemiro left Manchester United after four years this summer

Last Update:

Casemiro has joined Major League Soccer side Inter Miami following his departure from Manchester United.

The Brazilian midfielder left the Red Devils upon the expiry of his contract on June 30, ending a four-year spell at Old Trafford which saw him make 111 Premier League appearances and lift the FA Cup and Carabao Cup.

Having just returned from representing Brazil at the World Cup, the ex-Real Madrid star has now opted for a switch to MLS, where he will link up with Lionel Messi in the United States.

The former Manchester United star was officially unveiled by Miami on Wednesday after agreeing a deal through to the end of the 2027 MLS season, with the option to extend his stay until June 2029.

Casemiro joins Inter Miami.. but MLS investigate transfer

However, shortly after confirming the transfer, MLS released a statement revealing it had opened a review into a potential breach of league rules.

“The league is gathering all relevant information and will refrain from further comment until the review is complete,” the statement read.

MLS also confirmed that although Inter Miami and LA Galaxy had reached an agreement over Casemiro’s discovery rights, the details of that arrangement would not be disclosed until the investigation had concluded.

The probe centres on MLS’ discovery rights system, which allows clubs to claim priority over players who are not currently in the league.

Each MLS side can place up to five players on its discovery list at any one time, giving them the first opportunity to negotiate if one of those players decides to move to the United States.

LA Galaxy held Casemiro’s discovery rights before Inter Miami completed a deal to acquire them, paving the way for the experienced midfielder’s arrival in Florida.

Aston Villa agree loan deal for Chelsea flop following Rogers’ deal

He is set to join after a disappointing spell in west London.

Last Update:

Aston Villa have agreed to sign Alejandro Garnacho on an initial loan deal from Chelsea.

According to multiple reports, the two Premier League clubs have reached an agreement on a temporary deal that will become permanent if certain conditions are met.

Should the deal be made permanent, the 22-year-old will sign a four-year contract at Villa Park.

The news comes after Chelsea confirmed the signing of England attacking midfielder Morgan Rogers from Villa in a deal worth £117million, a record for a British player.

Garnacho’s arrival represents a gamble by Villa, whose squad has already changed significantly from the one that won the Europa League and finished fourth in the Premier League last season, securing a return to the Champions League.

In addition to Rogers, star midfielder Youri Tielemans departed for Manchester United, with Villa bringing in midfielder Joao Gomes and Switzerland World Cup star Johan Manzambi.

Garnacho, a Copa America winner in 2024, was not at the World Cup, having endured an underwhelming season with Chelsea following his move from Manchester United.

He scored just one goal and provided four assists in 24 Premier League appearances as the Blues limped to a 10th-place finish. Garnacho scored eight goals across all competitions.

However, Villa boss Unai Emery seemingly believes he can get the best out of Garnacho. For a side looking to continue on an upward trajectory after losing their prized asset, it is very important he is proven correct.

articles.title: Valverde hails ‘special person’ Mourinho as Real Madrid captain targets end to trophy drought
articles.summary: Skipper Valverde returned to training on Wednesday and had praise for the new Real Madrid boss.
articles.content:
Valverde hails ‘special person’ Mourinho as Real Madrid captain targets end to trophy drought

Skipper Valverde returned to training on Wednesday and had praise for the new Real Madrid boss.

Last Update:

Federico Valverde labelled Jose Mourinho as a “special person” as he stressed his desire to ensure the first season of the Real Madrid coach’s second spell in charge is one that results in trophies.

Valverde returned to Madrid’s training base for his first session under Mourinho on Wednesday.

The Madrid captain endured a disappointing World Cup with Uruguay as they crashed out in the group stage, failing to win any of their three games against Saudi Arabia, Cape Verde and eventual champions Spain.

But he is now firmly focused on the goal of adding to his tally of 14 trophies with Madrid, who suffered the rare ignominy of a trophy-less season last term in a tumultuous campaign that saw Valverde injured in a training ground bust-up with Aurelien Tchouameni in its closing stages.

Mourinho’s appointment as the successor to Alvaro Arbeloa raised eyebrows, but Valverde expressed excitement at the chance to play under the man who helped Madrid dethrone Pep Guardiola’s Barcelona in LaLiga in 2011-12.

“I’m really looking forward to learning from him, listening to every piece of advice he offers, and making the most of every second and minute of training I get to share with him and his coaching staff,” Valverde told Real Madrid TV.

“I want to learn and grow as both a person and a footballer. He is a special person I can learn a great deal from. I hope it’s a wonderful season.”

On his captaincy, Valverde added: “I feel a great sense of excitement and honour. Whenever someone on the street or within my circle mentions it, it truly fills me with pride and emotion.

“You reflect on everything that has happened — the good times and the bad — and now the moment has arrived for me to be the first captain. I learned so much from all the team-mates who served as captains here. They always offered incredible support, and I intend to build on that experience to grow alongside the coaching staff.

“This is the year I want to truly enjoy the game and give my absolute all—not just on the pitch, but off it as well—to ensure all my team-mates feel comfortable.

“It’s not just me; the whole team feels it. What we want most is to win trophies this year, to make the Madridistas happy so they can enjoy a season full of silverware and feel proud of us.”

Madrid will play their first unofficial game of Mourinho’s second spell when they face Albacete, who knocked Los Blancos out of the Copa del Rey last season, a week on Friday.

articles.content:
Gavi calls for Paredes to avoid suspension despite World Cup final bust-up

Gavi does not believe the incident should result in a ban.

Last Update:

Spain midfielder Gavi does not believe Argentina‘s Leandro Paredes should be suspended for his actions following the World Cup final.

There were ugly scenes at the end of last Sunday’s showpiece in New York/New Jersey, which Spain won 1-0 after extra time to clinch their second World Cup title.

Several Spain players were accosted by Argentina counterparts, with Leandro Paredes at the centre of the controversy as he grabbed Eric Garcia by the throat before pushing Gavi to the turf.

FIFA is set to open an investigation into Paredes’ conduct. Despite being on the receiving end of his behaviour, Barcelona midfielder Gavi does not wish to see the Boca Juniors player receive a ban.

“I don’t think [Paredes] should be suspended,” Gavi told El Partidazo de COPE.

“I understand it’s not a good image for children, but I think there’s also that side to football, which is a bit more physical, more aggressive.

“The most logical thing would have been to send him off during the match, and that’s it. In the end, I think it’s all football, and it has to be that way.”

It was initially incorrectly reported on FIFA’s commentator information system that referee Slavko Vincic had dismissed Paredes for his actions against Garcia.

However, the red card was deleted thereafter, and it has since been confirmed that no disciplinary action was taken by the match official.

Paredes is poised to play for Boca on Thursday when they face Chilean side O’Higgins in the Copa Sudamericana.

articles.title: Argentina coach Roberto Ayala to apologise to Dani Olmo in person but says clash was ‘a push, not a punch’
articles.summary: Roberto Ayala regrets his clash with Spain hero Dani Olmo following the World Cup final but the Argentina assistant coach insists no punches were thrown
articles.content:
Argentina coach Roberto Ayala to apologise to Dani Olmo in person but says clash was ‘a push, not a punch’

Roberto Ayala regrets his clash with Spain hero Dani Olmo following the World Cup final but the Argentina assistant coach insists no punches were thrown

Last Update:

Argentina assistant coach Roberto Ayala insists he did not punch Spain midfielder Dani Olmo following Sunday’s tempestuous World Cup final but has said he will apologise to the Barcelona star in person.

Ayala was involved in the post-match scuffles that marred the showpiece game in New Jersey with Argentina very much the aggressors as their frustration at losing 1-0 boiled over.

The former Napoli, AC Milan and Valencia defender, who was regarded as one of the most combative players of his generation, was embroiled in a scuffle with Olmo while Argentina midfielder Leandro Paredes grabbed Eric Garcia by the throat before pushing Gavi to the turf.

Speaking on Valencia Capital Radio, 53-year-old Ayala, who works under head coach Lionel Scaloni, said: “I saw there was a tussle in the middle of the field and we tried to look out for our players.

“I take full responsibility for my actions, my intention was to separate the players and nothing else. Sometimes things happen and you have a thousand pulses (in your body), but it’s not an excuse and the role I have is very important. I shouldn’t have done that no matter what I received.”

Table of Contents

It was a push, not a punch, insists Argentina coach Ayala

Regarding the alleged punch towards Olmo, he added: “It was more of a push than anything else, it was not a punch as they said. It was a reaction to something that was said but if I see Dani Olmo, I will apologise in person.”

Argentina’s conduct in the final – and the semi against England, after which they held up a hugely provocative banner relating to the Falkland Islands – has led to a tidal wave of criticism which Ayala finds strange.

“I don’t know why, I don’t know if it’s a campaign, but there was a certain animosity towards our team because we were doing well,” he added.

Ayala explains Argentina snub at trophy presentation

Argentina were also condemned for turning their backs on the trophy presentation, opting instead to face their supporters at one end of MetLife Stadium.

Ayala, who made 116 appearances for Argentina, said: “Now they are just looking for things to be negative about when it comes to Argentina. There were thousands of gestures from the Spanish players that weren’t highlighted. You have to do some real journalism.

“Most of our fans were there so we went to thank them for their sacrifice.”

articles.title: ‘Worth as much as the gold medal’ – Yamal reveals Messi message after Spain’s World Cup triumph over Argentina
articles.summary: Messi had words of wisdom for the man seen as his successor.
articles.content:
‘Worth as much as the gold medal’ – Yamal reveals Messi message after Spain’s World Cup triumph over Argentina

Messi had words of wisdom for the man seen as his successor.

Last Update:

Lamine Yamal revealed the words of advice he received from Lionel Messi following Spain‘s win over Argentina in last Sunday’s World Cup final.

Spain lifted the trophy for the second time in their history after an uninspiring final was settled by Ferran Torres’ extra-time strike.

Ugly scenes followed at the end, with several Spain players accosted by Argentina counterparts. Leandro Paredes was at the centre of the controversy, as he grabbed Eric Garcia by the throat before pushing Gavi to the turf. Paredes could yet face disciplinary action for his conduct, however, with FIFA set to open an investigation into his behaviour.

But there was sportsmanship on show between Argentina legend Messi and Yamal, seen as the man to assume his mantle at Barcelona after a phenomenal start to his club career.

The pair embraced on the pitch after the full-time whistle and, speaking to Marca, Yamal disclosed the motivational message Messi gave to the 19-year-old.

“He’s the greatest player in history and someone I’ve always looked up to,” Yamal said. “After the match, I wanted to show him my respect.

“He told me to keep following my path and that the future belongs to our generation.

“Those words are worth as much as the gold medal hanging around my neck.”

Yamal scored only one goal at the World Cup, which came in the group stage win over Saudi Arabia, and did not register an assist.

However, Yamal still had a great influence on Spain’s success with his undoubted physical ability and flair, completing more dribbles (35) than any other player at the tournament.

Having become the joint-fourth youngest player to win the World Cup at 19 years and six days, Yamal will be expected to be at the forefront of La Roja’s efforts to defend the European Championship in 2028 and the World Cup two years later, when the tournament will be co-hosted by Spain.

articles.title: Players from Argentine club Tigre display Malvinas flag after Copa Sudamericana win
articles.summary: Tigre could face action from CONMEBOL for displaying a flag that claimed the Falkland Islands were Argentine
articles.content:
Players from Argentine club Tigre display Malvinas flag after Copa Sudamericana win

Tigre could face action from CONMEBOL for displaying a flag that claimed the Falkland Islands were Argentine

Last Update:

Players from Argentine club Tigre displayed a flag relating to the Falkland Islands after a continental cup tie on Tuesday night in scenes reminiscent of those that followed the country’s World Cup semi-final win over England.

The incident came after Tigre’s 3-0 victory at Uruguayan side Nacional in the Copa Sudamericana play-offs. Visiting fans also sung the well-worn chant “who doesn’t jump is an Englishman”.

The Tigre players held up a flag that read: “Las Malvinas son Argentinas (The Falklands are Argentine).” The wording was the same as that displayed by Argentina’s players after they beat the Three Lions 2-1 in Atlanta last week

Britain and Argentina went to war over the Falklands in 1982, with the 74-day conflict resulting in the deaths of 649 Argentine soldiers, 255 British combatants and three civilians. The Falklands remain a British controlled territory, though Argentina insists the archipelago in the South Atlantic is its possession.

FIFA to investigate Argentina’s banner

FIFA is investigating the conduct of the national side and it remains to be seen if CONMEBOL, who operates the Copa Sudamericana, follows suit.

Tigre’s actions are unlikely to please the Falkland Islands Government, who last week said: “The Falkland Islands Government is disappointed – though regrettably not surprised – that the Argentine football team decided to tarnish the result of last night’s World Cup football semi-final – a game that did not in any case involve the Falkland Islands.

“That said, it is hardly news to anyone that the people of the Islands were victims of an aggressive invasion in 1982 which left many traumatised. The banner displayed by Argentina last night, therefore, was particularly insensitive for many people in the Falklands.

“It is the avowed policy of the Falkland Islands Government that we do not wish to see politics being brought into sport. Nor do we wish the Islands and their people to be used as a political football in every conversation about England and Argentina.”

Among the Argentina players holding up the Malvinas flag in the United States last week were Lisandro Martinez and Cristian Romero, who play for Manchester United and Tottenham respectively.

articles.title: Italy: ‘Exceptions’ being made to try to lure Guardiola to Azzurri job
articles.summary: Italy are attempting to convince Pep Guardiola to make his first foray into international coaching.
articles.content:
Italy: ‘Exceptions’ being made to try to lure Guardiola to Azzurri job

Italy are attempting to convince Pep Guardiola to make his first foray into international coaching.

Last Update:

Pep Guardiola is in talks about becoming the next Italy coach, with the president of the Italian Football Federation (FIGC) revealing that financial “exceptions” are being made to try to secure a deal.

Guardiola brought the curtain down on a 10-year spell as Manchester City manager in May.

The former Barcelona and Bayern Munich boss has never managed a national team, though he reportedly had an agreement with England in 2024 before changing his mind.

Italy are looking for a new coach after missing out on a third successive World Cup, the Azzurri failing to qualify for the 2026 tournament after losing a play-off final to Bosnia-Herzegovina on penalties.

Another former City manager, Roberto Mancini, is also in the running. Mancini led Italy to glory in Euro 2020. Meanwhile, former Italy midfielder Andrea Pirlo is under consideration despite his coaching career, which has seen spells with Juventus and Sampdoria, featuring little success to this point.

Guardiola is the standout name, but FIGC president Giovanni Malago stressed that him succeeding Gennaro Gattuso is no guarantee.

Malago told Cronache di Spogliatoio: “It’s not a given that this will come to fruition, but I believe it was right and important to open a dialogue and keep it alive.

“This [talks with Guardiola] is by no means a lack of respect towards other candidates, with whom discussions have already begun, and adding another name would in no way detract from the process.

“There are also financial and budgetary considerations. In the short to medium term, to say that we’ll have to tighten our belts is an understatement. However, some exceptions have been made, which may relate to the name that is so dominant at the moment: Pep Guardiola.”

Asked if Guardiola, Mancini and Pirlo are the only candidates for the vacant role, Malago replied: “Absolutely not. We think about a certain profile and certainly these names fall into that category.”

Having watched Spain win the 2026 World Cup from afar, Italy will return to action in September when they face Belgium in the UEFA Nations League. The Azzurri have been drawn in a difficult group that also features France and Turkey.

articles.title: BREAKING: Phil Foden signs new four-year contract at Manchester City
articles.summary: Phil Foden has extended his stay at Manchester City by signing a new, four-year deal at the Etihad
articles.content:
BREAKING: Phil Foden signs new four-year contract at Manchester City

Phil Foden has extended his stay at Manchester City by signing a new, four-year deal at the Etihad

Last Update:

Phil Foden has signed a new, four-year contract that will keep him at Manchester City until 2030, the club confirmed on Wednesday.

Foden, whose previous deal was due to expire next summer, joined City as a nine-year-old and has made 369 appearances for the club, helping them to 20 major trophies – a record he shares with Bernardo Silva and John Stones.

“Committing my future to City means everything to me,” he told the club’s official website.

“Playing for this club is all I’ve ever wanted to do and it’s always an honour to wear the shirt.  It’s not lost on me that I’ve been lucky enough to be part of a historic period with so many titles won, but we’re always looking to the future and trying to win more.

“I can only thank the club, staff, team-mates and fans who continue to put their faith in me and trust that I give everything I can for City and I hope I’ll be able to repay you for years to come.”

Table of Contents

Foden needs to prove qualities to new City boss Maresca

The forthcoming season is a big one for 26-year-old Foden with his former mentor Pep Guardiola having left and Enzo Maresca, who worked at City previously as Guardiola’s assistant during the 2022/23 treble-winning season, coming in as the new head coach.

Foden also has a point to prove after being left out of Thomas Tuchel’s England squad for the World Cup.

“I can’t wait to work with Enzo again. He was brilliant during the treble season – someone all the players respected and loved working with. To have him back here is exciting,” added Foden.

“Personally, I know I’ve improved so much from working with our coaches and world-class squad and as many of the legends who were here when I first broke through move on, I am excited for the next phase of my career at this great club.”

Foden is a ‘unique talent’ – City chief Viana

City’s director of football Hugo Viana is excited at what is still to come.

The Portuguese said: “Everyone at Manchester City is incredibly proud of Phil.

“He represents everything good about our academy. He is a unique talent, and his creativity is a joy to watch.

“But none of what he has achieved would be possible without the focus, dedication and humility to work hard in every moment and absorb all of the knowledge available to him through our coaches and players.

“Given Phil joined City at the age of nine, his continued success is one that is celebrated in every corner of our club from the academy staff who helped develop him right through to the City fans who have backed him throughout.

“At 26, his development is still ongoing,  and we look forward to seeing the player Phil can become  over the coming years.”

articles.title: Ipswich continue spending by snapping up Morocco international Issa Diop
articles.summary: Ipswich have made their sixth summer signing by bringing in central defender Issa Diop from Fulham
articles.content:
Ipswich continue spending by snapping up Morocco international Issa Diop

Ipswich have made their sixth summer signing by bringing in central defender Issa Diop from Fulham

Last Update:

Ipswich have continued their recruitment ahead of their return to the Premier League by signing Issa Diop from Fulham for a fee reported to be in the region of £8million.

The centre-half has significant top-flight experience having made 173 appearances for West Ham and Fulham and has signed a four-year deal at Portman Road.

Diop is Ipswich’s sixth summer signing as they look to make a better fist of life in the Premier League than in 2023/24 when they suffered an immediate return to the Championship.

The 29-year-old played in all five of Morocco’s games at the World Cup as the African champions reached the quarter-finals.

Ipswich boss Gary O’Neil told the club’s official website: “Issa is an experienced player who has played a significant amount of his career in the Premier League, so we’re delighted to have him with us.

“He is an imposing defender with good quality and a will to win, making him an excellent addition to the group.

“Having played and scored at the World Cup this summer, we’re looking forward to Issa joining up with the squad soon.”

Ipswich is the right place for me – Diop

Diop, who joins Abdul Fatawu, Emersonn and Kayne van Oevelen in moving to Suffolk this summer, as well as former loanees Cedric Kipre and Chuba Akpom whose deals have been made permanent, will join up with the squad following the training camp in La Manga.

“I’m excited to take the next step in my career at Ipswich Town,” said Diop.

“I know how big the club is and have enjoyed all of the conversations I have had before making the move. I know this is the right place for me.

“It has been a busy summer for me, representing Morocco at the World Cup, but I am proud to be joining Ipswich Town and am looking forward to meeting the staff, my teammates and the supporters very soon.”

Middlesbrough sign Spurs striker Lankshear in £20m deal

The striker will hope to help Middlesbrough return to the top flight.

Middlesbrough have completed the signing of striker Will Lankshear from Tottenham.

The Championship club confirmed the transfer after agreeing a reported fee of £10million with Spurs, with the deal also including a further £10m in add-ons.

Lankshear scored 11 goals in 43 appearances for Oxford United last season as he spent the 2025-26 campaign on loan at the Kassam Stadium, though he could not prevent Oxford suffering relegation to League One.

“Middlesbrough is such a massive club over the years; I deem it to be a Premier League club,” the 21-year-old told the club’s official website.

“The project here really excites me. I can’t wait to get started and be part of the journey, and get this club back where it belongs.

“I feel like now is the best time in my career. I’m ready to  hit the ground running and help this club.”

articles.title: FA charge Southampton boss Eckert following Spygate scandal
articles.summary: Southampton boss Tonda Eckert has been charged by the FA over the Spygate scandal and could be facing a severe sanction
articles.content:
FA charge Southampton boss Eckert following Spygate scandal

Southampton boss Tonda Eckert has been charged by the FA over the Spygate scandal and could be facing a severe sanction

Last Update:

Southampton boss Tonda Eckert has been formally charged with three breaches of FA regulations for his part in the Spygate scandal.

The Saints were expelled from the Championship play-offs in May after admitting to charges of spying on Middlesbrough ahead of their semi-final tie, which Southampton won 1-0, and ahead of regular-season games against Ipswich Town and Oxford United.

In addition to being kicked out of the play-off final against Hull City, Southampton were handed a four-point deduction for this coming season.

The club appealed, alleging the punishment was “manifestly disproportionate”. However, that claim was dismissed by an arbitration panel.

Table of Contents

Eckert key to Spygate scandal

Eckert was the central figure in the drama and had previously showed his frustration when discussing it, storming out of his post-match news conference following the second leg against Middlesbrough when asked if he was a cheat.

The German, who oversaw a remarkable upturn in Saints’ form after replacing Will Still in November, authorised the spying in what was described by an independent disciplinary commission as “a contrived and determined plan from the top down”.

Southampton have ruled out sacking him but the 33-year-old is likely to face a severe sanction, which may include a touchline ban.

An FA statement today read: “Southampton FC’s Tonda Eckert has been charged with three breaches of FA Rule E3.1 in relation to misconduct between December 2025 and May 2026. “It’s alleged that the head coach acted in an improper manner and/or brought the game into disrepute by directing and/or authorising the observation of training sessions of Oxford United FC, Ipswich Town FC and Middlesbrough FC ahead of fixtures between these clubs and Southampton FC in December 2025, April 2026 and May 2026 respectively.  “Tonda Eckert has until Tuesday 28 July 2026 to provide his responses.”

Eckert apologises for spying on opposition

Eckert said sorry for his actions in an emotional social media post in June.

Speaking to the club’s social media channels, he said: “What I’m going to say is not going to be perfect, but I will try to be as honest and clear as I can be.

“I think you deserve that. For everything that’s happened, I do want to apologise, and I hold my hand up because as a head coach, I am responsible.

“I am responsible for everything that has happened in this football club. I am responsible for everything that has happened in my coaching staff.

“I do apologise to the supporters, to everyone who has travelled with us, who has supported us over so many games.

“To the ones who have shared emotions game by game, who have managed to bring us all the way up to this very end of the season.

“We were supposed to play the biggest game of the season. I apologise to the players, who have done absolutely everything that they can.

“They have done absolutely everything in the last six months to bring this club back to where it belongs. They would have deserved to play the final.

“I apologise to all of the clubs that have been involved, and mostly I apologise to our supporters.”

Southampton owner Solak to stick with Eckert

Eckert will see Southampton’s fans over the next few weeks when they play pre-season games, although he is unlikely to be offered a warm reception, after club owner Dragan Solak said he would stand by the embattled 33-year-old.

Speaking to BBC Sport, the Serb said: “I think he deserves a second chance and I would give it to him. My full support would be behind him actually, because I think he’s a super-talented manager.

“I believe Tonda that he didn’t know that it was the rule that he was breaking.

“My personal opinion, and the opinion of the board, is that he is a manager who deserves to be backed by us and to be supported by us. I will obviously seek advice from the team. I will seek advice from the players, from the fans. But yes, if it’s ultimately my decision, he stays.”

Solak hopes Eckert will learn from his mistake and there will be no repeat.

He added: “I told him: ‘You almost broke my heart. You do it again, you’ll kill me. The next time I see you in July, if you don’t know the EFL book of rules by heart, you can’t work for me. Because, we can’t have another mistake.’

“I truly hope that he will learn from this experience and he will achieve an incredible career.”

articles.title: Disgraced Argentina midfielder Leandro Paredes set to play for Boca Juniors tomorrow night
articles.summary: Leandro Paredes has shunned a post-World Cup break and is set to return to action for Boca Juniors on Thursday night
articles.content:
Disgraced Argentina midfielder Leandro Paredes set to play for Boca Juniors tomorrow night

Leandro Paredes has shunned a post-World Cup break and is set to return to action for Boca Juniors on Thursday night

Last Update:

Leandro Paredes is poised to play for Boca Juniors on Thursday night, just four days after appearing in the World Cup final.

The Argentina midfielder came on at half-time in Sunday’s 1-0 defeat to Spain in New Jersey, playing 75 minutes as the game went to extra-time.

Paredes received widespread criticism after being involved in the disgraceful scenes at the final whistle that saw several Spain players physically assaulted by Argentines. Paredes was at the centre of the controversy, grabbing Eric Garcia by the throat before pushing Gavi to the turf.

It was widely reported that the 32-year-old had been sent-off for his actions but it later came to light that no action had been taken by referee Slavko Vincic. Paredes is still likely to face a sanction, though, with FIFA set to open an investigation into Argentina’s conduct.

The former PSG, Juventus and Roma man took to Instagram the day after the game but offered no apology.

He wrote: “Thank you Argentina! I love you today, and always.

“Today, I write with a heavy heart, having been unable to bring our country the joy it so richly deserves – but with a chest full of pride for having given everything we had and for flying our flag at the very top once again.

“Thank you to everyone who was part of this national team – to this group of players who gave their all to represent this jersey, fighting for it until the very last second of every match.

“It was an honour to be part of the best Argentine national team in history.”

Paredes trains with Boca

Having flown back to Argentina on Monday and joined in the celebrations that greeted the team’s return, Paredes immediately linked back up with the Boca squad at their Buenos Aires training complex.

Paredes was filmed working out in the gym and training with his team-mates ahead of the Copa Sudamericana clash with Chilean side O’Higgins at La Bombonera.

The Boca skipper has been named in the squad and is expected to start on the bench despite sustaining a minor rib injury during the World Cup.

articles.title: The fall of the greats is the joy of the mediocre – Lisandro Martinez lashes out at Argentina’s critics
articles.summary: Lisandro Martinez believes Argentina should receive more respect after reaching the World Cup final
articles.content:
The fall of the greats is the joy of the mediocre – Lisandro Martinez lashes out at Argentina’s critics

Lisandro Martinez believes Argentina should receive more respect after reaching the World Cup final

Last Update:

Lisandro Martinez and Alexis Mac Allister have both lashed out at Argentina’s critics who revelled in their World Cup final defeat to Spain.

The defending champions were beaten 1-0 in New Jersey on Sunday and produced an appalling display that was low on quality and high on gamesmanship before losing their discipline completely at the final whistle with several members of their playing and coaching staff lashing out at the Spaniards as they celebrated.

Their defeat was met with relief and joy from most neutrals but Manchester United defender Martinez, who had to come off just before half-time due to injury, claims their detractors should give Argentina more credit.

Writing on Instagram, he said: “It is heartbreaking not to have brought home the trophy we all wanted, yet I am filled with immense pride – pride in this jersey, my team-mates, the coaching staff, the management, the medical team, the cooks, the kit men, and everyone involved in making this whole journey run as smoothly as possible. And, above all, pride in you – for sending us all your love and strength, for sharing that passion that defines us so well, and for the unity of a country – a unity I hope endures.

“I want to congratulate Spain on their well-deserved title.

“To our people, I want to say that the result does not define the journey we took. We overcame adversity, made the impossible possible, and never sought excuses – we only found reasons to keep going. We defended our colours far beyond the pitch and shared unforgettable moments with the national team, alongside our families and with the unconditional support of all Argentines. It will always be a tremendous honour to represent you.

“Remember: ‘The fall of the greats is the joy of the mediocre.’ I love you, Argentina!”

Mac Allister thanks critics for providing Argentina with motivation

That defiance was echoed by Liverpool midfielder Mac Allister, who played the full 120 minutes at MetLife Stadium and produced a gritty display following the dismissal of Enzo Fernández.

Mac Allister said: “We were so close… that’s why it hurts so much. But no-one can take away everything we experienced during this World Cup. What they made us feel is extraordinary.

“We had to suffer, there were adversities, but we overcame them TOGETHER. Let’s never forget this, please: TOGETHER we are stronger than anyone.

“Let’s cry, because we’re Argentinians and we always want to win. But after crying, let’s get up, unite, and keep going, because this isn’t over. And these past few days, my mom reminded me of a popular saying: ‘If there’s a rematch, don’t be afraid.’

“Thank you to all Argentinians for every message of love and support. You don’t know how important you are on this journey. And thank you also to those from other countries who send us messages mocking or rejoicing in our pain.

“Without meaning to, you help us feel more and more proud to be Argentinian every day. THANK YOU ARGENTINA!”

articles.title: Donald Trump ready to endorse Gianni Infantino for the role of secretary-general of the United Nations
articles.summary: Donald Trump and Gianni Infantino struck up a close bond during the 2026 World Cup and the US president wants the FIFA chief to take on a more significant role
articles.content:
Donald Trump ready to endorse Gianni Infantino for the role of secretary-general of the United Nations

Donald Trump and Gianni Infantino struck up a close bond during the 2026 World Cup and the US president wants the FIFA chief to take on a more significant role

Last Update:

Donald Trump would like FIFA chief Gianni Infantino to become the next secretary-general of the United Nations.

Trump and Infantino have developed a close bond after working together to help the US deliver a successful World Cup, alongside Canada and Mexico, and the US president would like to see him play a greater role in politics moving forward.

According the New York Post, Infantino would be Trump’s preferred candidate to replace Antonio Guterres when the Portuguese steps down in December.

A source close to the president told the Post: “He [Infantino] is respected by everyone around the world, and [Trump] recognises he has a special ability to bring people together.”

Infantino, who awarded Trump FIFA’s inaugural Peace Prize in December, is thought to be happy in his current role and the reported £4.5million annual salary. But if he does throw his name into the hat to replace Guterres he would have to receive the endorsement of the 15-member UN Security Council and then the confirmation of the General Assembly.

Table of Contents

Infantino’s record shows he knows how to manage – US special envoy

Paolo Zampolli, Trump’s special envoy for global partnerships, told the Post: “Only President Trump could have such a genius idea.

“At the United Nations, you have to deal with 193 member states. In FIFA, there are over 200 members [and] Gianni’s great record shows he knows how to manage.”

Trump has been a frequent critic of the United Nations since returning for a second term as president and often voiced his frutration at their lack of intervention in global conflicts.

The Post speculates that having Infantino in a senior role at the UN would improve its relationship with the US.

Infantino continues to divide world football

Infantino remains a divisive figure in the world of football. While many confederations like the idea of an expanded World Cup that this year saw a record 48 teams take part, that view is not shared by many in Europe, who believe it dilutes the quality of the product.

The issue of hydration breaks also drew criticism, as did the extended half-time break in the final to allow the likes of Madonna, Justin Bieber and Shakira to perform.

Infantino was accused of fawning to Trump during the tournament when a conversation between the two led to the suspension of a red card awarded to USA striker Folarin Balogun in the round of 32 clash with Bosnia and Herzegovina.

Balogun was allowed to play in the subsequent game with Belgium but couldn’t prevent his side from losing 4-1.

articles.title: 2026 World Cup: Rating the 5 biggest achievers and underperformers at this summer’s tournament
articles.summary: Who were big hitters at the 2026 World Cup and which players flopped?
articles.content:
2026 World Cup: Rating the 5 biggest achievers and underperformers at this summer’s tournament

Who were big hitters at the 2026 World Cup and which players flopped?

Last Update:

Every World Cup produces two lists. The players who arrived with the weight of expectation and somehow exceeded it, and the ones who carried the same weight and crumbled.

The 2026 edition, for all its expanded format and logistical complexity, delivered both in abundance.

Spain won the tournament and produced plenty of standout performances, so did Argentina, France and England. Here are five from each side of the line.

Table of Contents

Five players who overachieved at the 2026 World Cup

Lionel Messi (Argentina)

He’s 39 and has been doing this since 2006, and somehow, in what is almost certainly his final World Cup, Messi produced the best individual tournament of any player on the planet.

Eight goals, four assists, 12 direct contributions, more than any other player at the tournament. His first World Cup hat-trick, in 31 appearances across six editions.

He broke Miroslav Klose’s all-time scoring record. He scored or assisted in 11 consecutive World Cup matches.

He has 10 knockout stage assists, six more than any other player in the recorded history of the competition.

Against England in the semi-final, with five minutes left and Argentina losing, he created two goals in the space of ten stoppage-time minutes.

At 39 years old, the age when most footballers are two or three years into retirement, Messi produced the most extraordinary individual World Cup performance since his own previous efforts.

Jude Bellingham (England)

Going into this tournament, there were questions about Bellingham. His club season at Real Madrid had been difficult, derailed by the chaos of Raul Arbeloa’s caretaker tenure and a lack of consistency that saw him in and out of the team at points during the campaign.

The World Cup offered a reset, and what followed was the most prolific individual tournament any midfielder has ever produced for the Three Lions.

Six goals across six matches, a seventh in the third-place match against France, four Man of the Match awards and a place in the record books as the highest-scoring midfielder in the history of the competition.

Erling Haaland (Norway)

This was Haaland’s first major international tournament, and he scored seven goals. A goal every 51 minutes. The best debut World Cup return since Grzegorz Lato’s seven for Poland in 1974.

He scored twice in the dying minutes to eliminate five-time champions Brazil in the last-16, the highlight of his summer.

His conversion rate of 39% from 18 shots was the best at a World Cup since Gary Lineker in 1986. Norway’s run ended in the quarter-finals, beaten 2-1 by England after extra time, but Haaland left North America with more World Cup goals from fewer matches than Messi, Ronaldo, Rooney or Zidane managed in their entire careers at the tournament.

Vozinha (Cape Verde)

The name means “Little Granny.” He did not turn professional until he was 25. He has played in Angola, Moldova, Portugal, Cyprus and Slovakia.

He was 40 years old when he ran out at MetLife Stadium for Cape Verde’s first-ever World Cup match against Spain and held the reigning European champions to a 0-0 draw with seven saves.

Over the course of the tournament, Vozinha made 18 saves, third most of any goalkeeper in the competition, and Cape Verde did not lose a single match in normal time.

They drew with Spain, Uruguay and Saudi Arabia before losing to Argentina 3-2 in extra time in the Round of 32, a match in which he made eight saves, including a miraculous stop on a Messi free kick in the 73rd minute.

By the time Cape Verde were eliminated, Vozinha had more Instagram followers than Manuel Neuer. Only Peter Shilton in 1990 and Dino Zoff in 1982 have made more World Cup saves at the age of 40 or above.

Rodri (Spain)

In September 2024, Rodri tore his ACL in a Manchester City match against Arsenal. He did not play competitive football again until February 2026.

He missed most of City’s season, watched them collapse domestically without him and arrived at the World Cup off the back of what was, by his standards, a limited competitive preparation.

What followed was the tournament of a man who had spent that time on the treatment table thinking about exactly how he would perform when the opportunity came.

He ranked first in Spain’s FIFA Power Rankings for the entire competition. His passing accuracy did not drop below 93% across seven matches.

He covered the ground that De la Fuente’s pressing system demanded, managed the tempo of every game Spain played and was, against Argentina in the final, the single reason that Scaloni’s side never found the rhythm they needed to threaten Unai Simon.

From ACL surgery to a World Cup winners’ medal in 18 months, he remains the game’s best defensive midfielder.

Five players who underachieved at the 2026 World Cup

Cristiano Ronaldo (Portugal)

He achieved his record. He became the first man to score in six World Cups and reached 27 appearances, second only to Messi in the all-time list.

Beyond those milestone numbers, however, Ronaldo’s tournament was a damning indictment of what he has become at international level.

He is the only forward to play 500 or more minutes across the 2022 and 2026 World Cups combined without completing a single successful dribble past an opponent.

Against DR Congo in the group stage opener, he had 16 touches and sent 17 of his 22 attempted passes backwards.

Against Spain in the last-16, when Portugal needed their most famous player to produce something, he was peripheral from start to finish as Mikel Merino’s 91st-minute winner ended their campaign.

Ronaldo finished with three goals across the tournament, two against Uzbekistan, one penalty, and Portugal, with Rafael Leao, Joao Felix and Pedro Neto available on the bench, went out having never fully unleashed the attacking quality that could have taken them further.

Bruno Fernandes (Portugal)

At club level, Bruno Fernandes had just broken the all-time Premier League assists record with Manchester United, providing 21 in a single season.

At the World Cup, the man who had been threading through balls and unlocking defences for the best part of nine months arrived on the international stage and produced almost nothing.

Portugal’s creative load fell almost entirely on younger shoulders, Joao Neves, in particular, was the most dynamic presence in the middle, while Fernandes struggled to impose himself on matches in the way his club form had suggested he would.

His no-show against Spain, where Portugal needed someone to create something and found the captain unable to provide it, was the defining image of his tournament.

Yan Diomande (Ivory Coast)

Before the tournament, the conversation around Yan Diomande centred on whether this was a breakout moment or simply the next step for a player who had already announced himself.

Twelve goals and eight assists for RB Leipzig in his debut Bundesliga season at 19 years old had placed him among the most watched young attackers in European football, with Liverpool, PSG and several other elite clubs monitoring his progress.

What the World Cup produced was a reminder of why senior international football at a major tournament is a different test entirely.

Diomande finished with one assist and zero goals across four matches, never able to impose his pace, directness and finishing quality at the level he had managed all season in the Bundesliga.

Ivory Coast beat Ecuador and Curacao in the group stage but were beaten by Germany and then knocked out by Norway in the Round of 32.

Kevin De Bruyne (Belgium)

Belgium’s golden generation has been trying to win a major tournament for a decade. At 35, De Bruyne arrived in North America for a final shot at adding an international trophy to an extraordinary club career.

The tournament he produced was difficult to reconcile with either the reputation or the Napoli form that had earned him his place in the squad.

Belgium drew with Croatia, Egypt and Iran across a stuttering group stage, with De Bruyne admitting to “silly mistakes” and suggesting his side had “put a lot of pressure on themselves.”

The most damning moment came in the last-16 against the United States, Belgium’s biggest match of the tournament.

Rudi Garcia dropped him entirely from the starting lineup. Belgium won 4-1 without him. He returned as captain for the quarter-final against Spain, but by then the momentum was gone, and Belgium lost 2-1.

Joshua Kimmich (Germany)

Germany came to North America with genuine optimism. Nagelsmann had rebuilt the squad, Wirtz and Musiala offered the creative quality that had been missing for years, and a 7-1 opening demolition of Curacao briefly suggested the drought of major tournament success was about to end. It did not.

Germany failed to produce their best football against any opponent, and when Paraguay held them 1-1 in the Round of 32 before winning on penalties, it was a third consecutive World Cup elimination before the quarter-finals.

Kimmich, as captain, delivered the most honest post-match assessment of anyone at the tournament. “We didn’t play well against any opponent. Three times we had major problems against teams that aren’t world-class. That’s a fact. We deserved to be eliminated.”

He will be 35 at the 2030 World Cup, and the window he wanted to use to win something for Germany has now closed.

articles.title: Morgan Rogers completes £117m Chelsea transfer as Arsenal miss out on Aston Villa midfielder
articles.summary: Chelsea have signed England midfielder Morgan Rogers from Villa
articles.content:
Morgan Rogers completes £117m Chelsea transfer as Arsenal miss out on Aston Villa midfielder

Chelsea have signed England midfielder Morgan Rogers from Villa

Last Update:

Chelsea have signed Morgan Rogers from Aston Villa for £117m on a six-year deal after the England midfielder reportedly turned down Arsenal to work with new Blues head coach Xabi Alonso.

The Midlands club confirmed their star man’s departure in a statement on social media, saying: “Aston Villa can confirm that Morgan Rogers has completed a permanent transfer to Chelsea.

“Since joining from Middlesbrough in 2024, the midfielder has enjoyed a rapid rise to prominence, helping Villa to lift the UEFA Europa League last term, scoring the third goal in the final in Istanbul.

“During his time at the club, he also earned his first senior England caps, representing his country at the FIFA World Cup 2026, where the Three Lions finished third.

“A player with impeccable behaviour and commitment, Morgan leaves Aston Villa with the best wishes of everyone at the football club for both his service to the club and for his future career. He will always remain a core part of our recent great moments and memories.”

Speaking for the first time as a Chelsea player, Rogers added: “I’m so excited; for me, Chelsea are the biggest club in London and a club I’ve always admired since I was a kid.

“I’m really excited about the project with the new manager, the players we’ve got and where the club is heading. That’s why I’m here and I can’t wait to get started.”

Table of Contents

Morgan Rogers stats: Aston Villa, Middlesbrough

Born in Halesowen in the West Midlands, Rogers spent nine years at nearby West Bromwich Albion’s academy before joining Manchester City, winning the 2019/20 FA Youth Cup.

He had loan spells with Lincoln City, Bournemouth and Blackpool and then joined Middlesbrough permanently, scoring seven goals to help Boro finish eighth in the Championship and reach the EFL Cup semi-finals in 2023/24.

Villa signed Rogers for an initial £8 million in February 2024 and he swiftly established himself as an important figure for Unai Emery’s team, proceeding to contribute 14 goals and 15 assists across all competitions in 2024/25, including a hat-trick in a Champions League victory against Celtic.

Those numbers earned Rogers the Villa and PFA Young Player of the Year honours, and he added 14 goals and 11 assists in 2025/26, winning the Europa League Player of the Season award as Villa lifted the trophy.

No English player bettered Rogers’ total of 84 attempts at goal in the 2025/26 Premier League, while no midfielder eclipsed his tally of 32 on target.

His goals-vs-expected-goals total of 3.22 was also the eighth-highest of any player in the division, helped by Rogers’ talent for spectacular strikes.

Morgan Rogers England career: World Cup starter

An England regular at youth level between the ages of 14 and 21, Rogers made his senior debut away to Greece in the Nations League in November 2024.

Lee Carsley, who was interim England head coach following Gareth Southgate’s exit, gave Rogers his bow and current boss Thomas Tuchel has continued to pick him since becoming Southgate’s permanent successor at the start of 2025.

Rogers scored his only Three Lions goal in a 3-0 friendly win at home to Wales in October 2025 and was called up for the World Cup 2026, appearing in seven of England’s eight matches at the finals.

A full World Cup debutant against Panama during the group stage, Rogers played throughout England’s semi-final defeat to Argentina – crossing for Anthony Gordon to open the scoring – and third-place play-off win over France.

When will Morgan Rogers make his Chelsea debut?

Here’s how Chelsea’s pre-season schedule looks.

When does Chelsea’s Premier League 2026/27 season start?

Chelsea’s Premier League season begins away to Fulham on Monday, August 24 at 20:00 BST.

In the UK, the game will be shown live on Sky Sports Main Event, Premier League and Ultra, with streaming via Sky Go.

articles.summary: Crysencio Summerville is set to join Saudi Pro League side Al Hilal this summer.
articles.content:
West Ham’s Summerville set for Saudi switch amid Aston Villa interest

Crysencio Summerville is set to join Saudi Pro League side Al Hilal this summer.

Last Update:

Saudi Pro League side Al-Hilal have agreed a £68.3 million deal with West Ham to sign winger Crysencio Summerville.

The 24-year-old Netherlands international has been offered a long-term contract and has been given permission to undergo a medical ahead of completing the move.

West Ham had previously rejected an offer worth around £40 million for Summerville, who also attracted interest from Aston Villa, but the Riyadh-based club have now reached an agreement with the Championship side.

The transfer represents another significant financial boost for West Ham following their relegation from the Premier League in May.

The Hammers sold midfielder Mateus Fernandes to Tottenham for £85 million last month, while captain Jarrod Bowen has committed his future to the club by signing a revised contract despite their drop into the second tier.

With the club looking to reduce its wage bill and generate funds following relegation, Summerville’s departure continues a summer of major player sales.

West Ham have retained manager Nuno Espirito Santo as they prepare for the 2026-27 Championship campaign, with promotion back to the Premier League their primary objective.

articles.title: IShowSpeed plays football in World Cup 2026 video as Cristiano Ronaldo fan faces JasonTheWeen, Marlon, Sean Garnier, Zias, Brittany Isenhour and Freda Ayisi: ‘Shout out to FIFA’
articles.summary: IShowSpeed lifted a version of the World Cup trophy
articles.content:
IShowSpeed plays football in World Cup 2026 video as Cristiano Ronaldo fan faces JasonTheWeen, Marlon, Sean Garnier, Zias, Brittany Isenhour and Freda Ayisi: ‘Shout out to FIFA’

IShowSpeed lifted a version of the World Cup trophy

Last Update:

Cristiano Ronaldo devotee IShowSpeed has shown off his own football skills in a video shot in New York’s Central Park with a squad of fellow influencers.

Streamers JasonTheWeen and Marlon, YouTuber Zias, former professional player Brittany Isenhour, Watford goalkeeper Freda Ayisi and freestyler Sean Garnier took part in a match during the World Cup 2026, with two-time world champion Cafu and legendary referee Pierluigi Collina providing expertise.

“I enjoyed this World Cup a lot,” said IShowSpeed, whose real name is Darren Jason Watkins Jr and is also known as Speed.

“More than the last World Cup [in Qatar in 2022], 100%. Just everybody’s emotion, everybody’s compassion.

“Before the game, I hang out even before [getting to] the stadium. I chill with the fans. It’s just a fun atmosphere and a fun vibe.”

Table of Contents

Marlon, Sean Garnier, Zias: World Cup 2026 ‘a shock’

Swedish internet celebrity Marlon called co-hosting country the US “a very good place” to stage the finals because of the “different cultures and different people all in the same place”.

“People have seen that,” reflected the 24-year-old. “It’s been a shock to everyone. I’m seeing TikTok posts or Instagram posts from people who have never been into it.

“Now they’re watching every single game. It’s been really good.”

French former professional and world champion freestyler Garnier echoed Marlon’s words on inclusivity, while Zias admitted he has become hooked on football.

“I’m not a big, avid soccer fan,” said the American. “This is probably the most I’ve paid attention to it and I feel like I’ve been missing out. It’s a lovely sport and I’m having fun.”

IShowSpeed: Brittany Isenhour backs World Cup football

Ex-United States youth international goalkeeper Isenhour described seeing the World Cup in her homeland as “so cool”.

“I feel like my dream as a professional soccer player was sparked when I watched the women play in my home town,” reflected the 28-year-old.

“So to see so many other kids getting to see their idols play in the US, so many other dreams will be sparked.”

Iconic full-back Cafu said the World Cup is “about bringing people together while being treated equally”.

“It makes you hug, raise a glass and argue with people you’ve never met before,” he suggested. “That’s the power of a World Cup.

“That’s the kind of message the World Cup should be promoting – one of peace and inclusion.”

IShowSpeed shouts out FIFA and YouTube at World Cup

Despite seeing Ronaldo knocked out in the last 16 by Spain, IShowSpeed was able to mimic lifting and kissing the trophy with a version of the prize at the end of the event in the park.

“A great shout out to Cafu,” he said, embracing the most-capped Selecao player of all time. “He was our manager.

“We did our thing. Shout-out to everybody on our team, to FIFA, to YouTube. It was great.

“Any country, any city, any town you go to – if it’s a football there and you pass it to them, they’ll pass the ball right back to you.”

IShowSpeed performed at the final in New Jersey on July 19, when the reigning European champions beat holders Argentina 1-0 after extra time.

articles.title: Aston Villa in advanced talks to sign Chelsea’s Garnacho
articles.summary: Aston Villa are closing in on a deal for Alejandro Garnacho from Chelsea.
articles.content:
Aston Villa in advanced talks to sign Chelsea’s Garnacho

Aston Villa are closing in on a deal for Alejandro Garnacho from Chelsea.

Last Update:

Aston Villa are in advanced talks to sign Chelsea winger Alejandro Garnacho on an initial loan deal that could include an obligation to buy.

The 21-year-old Argentina international was made available for transfer last month, with Chelsea initially valuing him at £43 million. While the Blues remain open to a permanent sale, discussions have centred on a deal that would see Garnacho join Villa on loan before a permanent move is triggered under agreed conditions.

Talks between the clubs have intensified following Chelsea’s club-record £117 million signing of Morgan Rogers from Villa that is set to complete in the coming days.

Garnacho and striker Nicolas Jackson, who is valued at £65 million, were both discussed as part of separate negotiations that could see the pair move to Villa Park.

If the deal is completed, Garnacho would become Villa’s fourth signing of the summer, following the arrivals of Johan Manzambi, Joao Gomes and Modou Kaba Cisse.

Villa have also raised close to £200 million through player sales during the window, with Youri Tielemans, Donyell Malen, Enzo Barrenechea and Lewis Dobbin all departing.

Chelsea have been willing to listen to offers for Garnacho despite signing him from Manchester United for £40 million only last September. United are entitled to 10% of any future transfer fee.

The winger has struggled to establish himself at Stamford Bridge, scoring just once in the Premier League, while the arrivals of Rogers and Sporting winger Geovany Quenda have increased Chelsea’s desire to trim their squad ahead of the new season.

articles.title: Anthony Taylor retires as referee after 831-game stint
articles.summary: Premier League referee Anthony Taylor is retiring from football
articles.content:
Anthony Taylor retires as referee after 831-game stint

Premier League referee Anthony Taylor is retiring from football

Last Update:

Anthony Taylor has announced his immediate retirement from refereeing, bringing the curtain down on a distinguished 20-year career.

The 47-year-old’s final match was Spain’s 1-0 win over Portugal in the World Cup round of 16 on July 6.

Taylor, who worked as a prison officer before becoming a professional referee, joined the Football League list ahead of the 2006-07 season and was promoted to the Premier League in 2010.

Over his career, he officiated 668 professional matches in England, including 432 Premier League fixtures, and took charge of every major domestic cup final.

“Officiating at the elite level has been an immense privilege, but the pressure is intense and the scrutiny is constant,” Taylor said.

“The time is now right to step aside and look forward to transitioning to the next chapter of my career.”

Taylor also enjoyed an extensive international career, spending 14 years on FIFA’s list of referees. He officiated at the 2022 World Cup, Euro 2020 and Euro 2024, while overseeing 163 international matches.

He was shortlisted to referee the 2022 World Cup final but was ultimately overlooked because of political tensions involving finalists Argentina.

Webb pays tribute to Taylor

Howard Webb, chief refereeing officer at Pro Ref, paid tribute to Taylor’s contribution to the game.

“Anthony has been a fantastic servant to football over many years, both domestically and on the international stage,” Webb said.

“He has been repeatedly trusted to officiate in the biggest games.

“We thank him for his immense contribution to the game and wish him every success in the next chapter of his career.”

Among Taylor’s most notable appointments were the 2015 EFL Cup final, two FA Cup finals in 2017 and 2020, the 2015 Community Shield and the 2018 Championship play-off final.

He also refereed several major UEFA fixtures, including the 2020 Super Cup, the 2021 Nations League final and the 2023 Europa League final.

Taylor received widespread praise for his handling of Denmark’s Euro 2020 match against Finland after Christian Eriksen suffered a cardiac arrest on the pitch.

One of the most challenging moments of his career came after the 2023 Europa League final, when then-Roma manager Jose Mourinho labelled him “a disgrace” before confronting him in a car park. Mourinho later received a four-match ban for the incident.

Taylor and his family were also subjected to abuse from supporters at Budapest Airport following the match.

articles.title: Argentina star attacks ‘unfounded conspiracy theories’ over World Cup: ‘I see how many people hoped for this defeat’
articles.summary: Rodrigo De Paul and Leandro Paredes have reacted after the World Cup final
articles.content:
Argentina star attacks ‘unfounded conspiracy theories’ over World Cup: ‘I see how many people hoped for this defeat’

Rodrigo De Paul and Leandro Paredes have reacted after the World Cup final

Last Update:

Argentina midfielder Rodrigo De Paul says accusations of favouritism towards his country at the World Cup 2026 were made up to “soothe the pain of others who couldn’t experience what all Argentinians were experiencing”.

The 2022 champions lost to Spain after extra-time in the final on Sunday, having won a series of close knockout-stage matches and faced allegations from Egypt boss Hossam Hassan that organisers FIFA wanted Albiceleste captain Lionel Messi and his team “to stay in the running”.

“The greatest pain is that we couldn’t bring the World Cup back to our country, because if anyone deserved to relive that feeling, it was you,” De Paul told Argentina’s fans.

“Today, I see how many people were hoping for this defeat, spreading unfounded conspiracy theories throughout the World Cup to soothe the pain of others who couldn’t experience what all Argentinians were experiencing.

“[It’s] because our smiles bother them, because our mannerisms annoy them… but that only reaffirmed that the passion and love for our jersey can overcome anything.”

Table of Contents

World Cup 2026: Why Argentina faced accusations

Hassan called for the match officiating team to be removed from the finals and claimed Egypt had been “treated unfairly” and “suffered injustice” following his side’s last-16 defeat, having been 2-0 ahead in the 78th minute and had a goal ruled out.

In Argentina’s opening match of the tournament, captain Messi scored a hat-trick but might have been sent off early on for catching Algeria counterpart Aissa Mandi on the calf and Achilles, with the USA’s Folarin Balogun shown a red card for a similar challenge later in the group stage.

Switzerland had just equalised against Argentina in the quarter-finals when Nati forward Breel Embolo was dismissed for simulation, leading to suggestions that the outcome may have misapplied protocols.

Argentina did not receive any cautions for a string of strong early fouls during their semi-final win over England, with the move for their winner bearing similarities to Egypt’s disallowed goal against them.

“As the hours go by, you’re [fans] making us realise that your connection with this team goes far beyond the trophy,” said De Paul, who is also a teammate of Messi at MLS club Inter Miami.

“That’s something I want to hold onto to get through this moment. It will hurt for a long time but, today more than ever, I am proud to be Argentine.”

Argentina vs Spain: Paredes reacts to World Cup final

Midfielder Leandro Paredes was at the centre of unedifying scenes immediately after the final, pushing Spain counterpart Gavi to the ground in the most noticeable altercation as players from either side attacked each other on the pitch.

Ferran Torres scored the 106th-minute winner after Argentina’s Enzo Fernandez received a second booking during regular time.

“I love you today and always,” Paredes told fans. “I write with a heavy heart for not being able to give you the joy our country so deserves.

“But my heart is bursting with pride for giving everything we had and raising our flag high once again.

“Thank you to everyone who was part of this team; to this group of players,who gave their all to represent this jersey, just like they did until the very last second of every match.

“It was an honour to be part of the best Argentine national team in history.”

World Cup 2026 conspiracy theories: What referees said

FIFA’s chief refereeing officer, Pierluigi Collina, said the integrity of the match officials at the tournament was unquestionable.

“Of course, constructive discussion about decisions will always be part of football, but unfounded allegations have no place in our sport,” Collina said after Argentina beat Egypt, warning that such claims “may provoke reactions that lead to threats against [officials] and their families”.

“This is not right,” he added. “Equally, nobody can claim that FIFA refereeing can be influenced by anyone – not even by the FIFA president [Gianni Infantino].

“He [Infantino] has always shown his full support for [the World Cup 2026 officials] while trusting us to work with complete independence.

“Match officials make honest decisions and, just like players and coaches, they always try to do their best.”

World Cup referee: Claims of bias ‘nonsense’

Writing before this year’s final, Darren Cann, who was an assistant for the 2010 showpiece, said referees are “completely distinct from FIFA”.

“According to many fans, social media timelines and corners of the internet, FIFA wants Argentina and Lionel Messi to win the World Cup and the officials are all in on it,” Cann told BBC Sport.

“As referees, we are forced to deal with the idea that we are part of some kind of conspiracy theory all the time.

“It is nonsense. I can’t stress this strongly enough. I can’t think of many other professions in the world where there is one person with all that pressure on them.

“The referee is making multi-million-pound decisions and they have got one second to make their mind up.

“Mistakes have been made on the pitch, of course they have. But they do not add up to a conspiracy.

Englishman Cann addressed a rumour he had heard about that FIFA “wanted an Argentina vs Spain final to create a passing of the baton between Messi and [Spain’s] Lamine Yamal”.

“The suggestion that referees are in on some kind of masterplan to make sure Messi gets to the final is just not true, obviously,” he said.
