articles.title: Premier League: The ONE player your club should sign this summer
articles.summary: Nico Williams is one player we would love to see in the Premier League next season but who should sign him?
articles.content:
Premier League: The ONE player your club should sign this summer

Nico Williams is one player we would love to see in the Premier League next season but who should sign him?

Last Update:

The World Cup is over and the wait for the domestic game to return is now underway.

The EFL re-starts on Friday, August 14 and the Premier League a week later when champions Arsenal host newly promoted Coventry.

Between now and then there is bound to be frantic transfer activity as clubs attempt to bolster their squads before the big kick-off.

Here, we identify one signing that each club should make in the summer window.

Table of Contents

ARSENAL

With Morgan Rogers seemingly heading for Chelsea, sporting director Andrea Berta will have to train his focus elsewhere. The sale of Leandro Trossard now appears slightly misjudged and the Gunners will surely be in the market for a winger. Nico Williams endured an injury-interrupted season with Athletic Bilbao in 2025/26 but showed his quality off the bench in the World Cup final. Has a release clause of around £80million which would not be a problem. If he can stay fit, the 24-year-old would be tailor-made for the Premier League.Target: Nico Williams

ASTON VILLA

It is another busy summer at Villa Park as the club try to move forward while complying with financial regulations. Rogers’ departure is a blow, albeit one softened slightly by the arrivals of Joao Gomes and Johan Manzambi. Villa are reportedly willing to let Ollie Watkins go but that would leave them desperately short of striking options. Nicolas Jackson would be the ideal replacement. The 25-year-old Senegal international needs to feel loved after two largely underwhelming seasons at Chelsea and Bayern Munich and, if he does, he could help fire Villa to a top-four finish.Target: Nicolas Jackson

BOURNEMOUTH

The Cherries need defenders following the departures of Marcos Senesi and Alex Jimenez. Aaron Wan-Bissaka is not the kind of up-and-coming player Bournemouth normally target but he would be a very solid, relatively low-cost option from relegated West Ham.Target: Aaron Wan-Bissaka

BRENTFORD

Brentford have made a couple of eye-catching moves this summer, but only because they have a different profile from the kind of player they usual go for. Bringing in Jaidon Anthony from Burnley was a surprise move but not as shocking as signing 34-year-old Callum Wilson from West Ham. Cologne winger Said El Mala was linked earlier in the summer and his signing would be a real coup with Borussia Dortmund also interested.Target: Said El Mala

BRIGHTON

Brighton’s famed algorithm reportedly led to them agreeing terms with El Mala in April, although they are said to have disagreed with Cologne over his value and the 19-year-old Germany youth winger has joined pre-season training with the Bundesliga club. Albion will perhaps look to add more experience following the departures of James Milner, Joel Veltman, Solly March and coach Andrew Crofts, with John Stones a dream signing for fans but likely too much of a coup right now. Finding a forward as prolific and classy as Danny Welbeck looks as urgent as ever with a potentially long European campaign expanding the schedule. The answer could come from within the squad, with Georginio Rutter a work in progress in the Premier League and prospects Charalampos Kostoulas and Stefanos Tzimas hoping to prove themselves.Target: Said El Mala

CHELSEA

Chelsea’s endless spending shows no sign of slowing down with Rogers set to join Marco Palestra and Geovany Quenda at Stamford Bridge this summer. Chelsea were also interested in Granit Xhaka before Sunderland ruled out any chance of their captain leaving Wearside. With Chelsea’s owners promising to bring in ‘Premier League-ready’ players this summer, new boss Xabi Alonso would love some older heads. England international Stones would be a perfect fit in a defence that often creaked last season.Target: John Stones

COVENTRY CITY

Coventry must recruit heavily and recruit well. The formula on how to stay in the Premier League following promotion was outlined by Sunderland and Leeds last season with both clubs surviving with ease. An obvious position they need to recruit in is goalkeeper with the on-loan Carl Rushworth returning to parent club Brighton after playing a key role in their Championship title success. Reports suggest the 25-year-old is desperate to rejoin the Sky Blues and this seems a no-brainer for boss Frank Lampard.Target: Carl Rushworth

CRYSTAL PALACE

Palace have had some high-profile departures in recent years – Michael Olise and Eberechi Eze, for example – and it seems Maxence Lacroix could well join them with Chelsea sniffing round the France international. If Lacroix does leave Selhurst Park then Palace will need a commanding central defender to fill the void. Chelsea have reportedly made Trevoh Chalobah available for transfer. The former Palace loanee would be an ideal fit.Target: Trevoh Chalobah

EVERTON

Everton are a classic David Moyes team; honest, workmanlike but lacking in star quality. Jack Grealish brought it in the first half of last season before injury struck. A permanent deal to bring Grealish back to the Hill Dickinson Stadium is a possibility but Everton may be better looking at his Manchester City team-mate Savinho. Blessed with more pace, the Brazilian would immediately bolster Everton’s attacking options, albeit he wouldn’t come cheap.Target: Savinho

FULHAM

One of the most intriguing appointments of the summer was Alvaro Arbeloa’s at Fulham. The former Spain international did not have the most successful spell in charge of Real Madrid last season but was not helped by a dressing room riddled with cliques and in-fighting. Arbeloa is reportedly eager to bring one of Madrid’s starlets with him to Craven Cottage and Gonzalo Garcia would be a shrewd acquisition to replace Raul Jimenez who has rejoined Wolves.Target: Gonzalo Garcia

HULL CITY

Hull are an even more exaggerated version of Coventry. They need a better quality of player in multiple positions although their spending power is likely to be restricted by financial regulations. Free agents and loan moves could be the order of the day and one eye-catching name that has been mentioned is Paris Saint-Germain midfielder Renato Sanches, whose career is in need of rebuilding after he burst on to the scene as a teenager.Target: Renato Sanches

IPSWICH TOWN

Ipswich recruited heavily the last time they were promoted but targeted top-end Championship players in a policy that ultimately failed. The pursuit of centre-half Issa Diop from Fulham suggests they may have learned their lesson but the Morocco centre-half will need to be accompanied by several more experienced Premier League players if they are to survive. New boss Gary O’Neill could do worse than to return to his old club Wolves and snap up Brazil international midfielder Andre, even though he has recently signed a new deal at Molineux.Target: Andre

LEEDS UNITED

Leeds have already signed Harry Wilson and Bosnia and Herzegovina defender Tarik Muharemovic this summer as they look to build on their encouraging return to the top flight last season. The departures of Illan Meslier and Karl Darlow mean they require a goalkeeper. Lucas Perri was hit and miss in his first year at Elland Road and boss Daniel Farke must decide whether to place his faith in the 28-year-old or dip into the market. James Trafford endured a frustrating season at Manchester City last year and could be tempted to make the short move across the M62.Target: James Trafford

LIVERPOOL

Liverpool will hope the arrival of Andoni Iraola will spark an upturn in fortunes following the exit of Arne Slot. Iraola inherits a strong squad but one that needs tweaking. Left-wing has repeatedly been flagged as a position that requires strengthening but with Cody Gakpo, Hugo Ekitike and Florian Wirtz all capable of playing there – not to mention burgeoning talent Rio Ngumoha – there seems little need to invest. Liverpool were often overrun in midfield last season and it may be Iraola returns to his former club Bournemouth in a bid to sign Alex Scott, who has turned down a new contract with the Cherries.Target: Alex Scott

MANCHESTER CITY

City continue to spend while the football world awaits the verdict from an independent commission into allegations the club breached multiple financial rules. Elliot Anderson is the latest big-money arrival, joining from Nottingham Forest for £116m. It’s hard to pick any holes in the City squad but, if there is one area of possible weakness, it is at centre-half with John Stones and Nathan Ake both leaving. City like to sign young players and bring them on which is why Crystal Palace’s Jaydee Canvot, 19, would be the perfect project.Target: Jaydee Canvot

MANCHESTER UNITED

United have been active since the window opened, bringing in midfielders Andrey Santos and Youri Tielemans. Their squad has a nice balance to it, although they are still lacking at right-back with Diego Dalot their only senior option. United could do a lot worse than try to prise Ben White from Arsenal, although William Saliba’s back injury could complicate matters.Target: Ben White

NEWCASTLE UNITED

After the departures of Anthony Gordon and Sandro Tonali, it is imperative Newcastle keep hold of captain Bruno Guimaraes. If the Brazilian leaves for Arsenal then it will open up a huge hole in midfield. A new transfer model that targets younger players has been implemented this summer but Newcastle still need some experience in the middle of the park. He may not be a flashy option but Christian Norgaard was one of the better holding midfielders in the Premier League while at Brentford. Given his limited playing time at Arsenal, he would likely relish a move to the North East.Target: Christian Norgaard

NOTTINGHAM FOREST

Having lost Anderson to City, Forest are in need of a strong central midfielder to plug the gap. Liverpool’s Curtis Jones could be the ideal replacement. The 25-year-old was expected to join Inter Milan but a disagreement over the fee has seen the move thrown into doubt. Forest could, and should, step in. Jones has a similar profile to Anderson and would also give Forest money to play with.Target: Curtis Jones

SUNDERLAND

One of the stories of last season was Sunderland’s remarkable seventh-placed finish just a year after promotion via the play-offs. The challenge now is to build on that success and cope with the additional fixtures thrown up by playing in the Europa League. Sunderland are known to be looking for a left-footed right winger and one name is consistently mentioned: Amad Diallo. The Ivory Coast star had a hugely successful loan spell on Wearside in the 2022/23 season and remains a popular figure at the Stadium of Light. He won’t come cheap with Manchester United eager to retain Diallo but his signing would be a real statement of intent.Target: Amad Diallo

TOTTENHAM

Spurs have been the most active team in the window so far as they look to improve on two successive 17th-placed finishes. They appear certain to better that record next season under Roberto De Zerbi, who has already signed the likes of Andy Robertson, Marcos Senesi, Tonali and Mateus Fernandes. The squad still requires a reliable goalscorer, though, and Bournemouth’s Eli Kroupi Jr has been mentioned as a potential target. The gifted 20-year-old was hugely impressive at the Vitality Stadium last season and would form a major piece of the De Zerbi jigsaw.Target: Eli Kroupi Jr

articles.title: Vinicius Jr rocks new look after chin surgery (yes, it’s really him…)
articles.summary: Vinicius Jr looks like a new man after chin reconstruction surgery
articles.content:
Vinicius Jr rocks new look after chin surgery (yes, it’s really him…)

Vinicius Jr looks like a new man after chin reconstruction surgery

Last Update:

Real Madrid winger Vinicius Jr is sporting a radically different look after undergoing chin surgery.

The Brazil international is reported to have had the procedure in his homeland following his country’s round of 16 exit to Norway at the World Cup.

Vinicius has had chin harmonisation surgery which “uses fillers to sculpt the facial contour” and giving more definition to the bottom of the face.

The results are remarkable with the 26-year-old looking very little like the player who was previously one of the most recognisable in world football.

Table of Contents

Vinicius rocks new look alongside girlfriend

His new look emerged on the Instagram page of his on-off girlfriend Virginia Fonseca, with Vini accompanying her on the opening of her new gym.

A video has also emerged of the player wishing a fan happy birthday.

Vinicius will shortly be returning to Spain to start his pre-season in Madrid under new boss Jose Mourinho.

The Brazil international’s current contract expires in 12 months’ time, leaving the club vulnerable to one of their most valuable players walking away on a free transfer in 2027.

And while the winger insists there is mutual trust on finding a resolution, he does not appear in a rush to sign a new deal.

Speaking to Caze TV in May, he said: “I have never imagined myself outside Real Madrid. I take advantage of every minute I am here because it is the club of my dreams.

“Now I am one of the captains, and that is very important. I want to stay here my whole life. I have to speak with Madrid and Madrid has to speak with me. The club is calm and I am calm. The president trusts me and I trust him. We will wait.”

We failed last season, admits Real Madrid star Vinicius

Hopes are high for a better season at the Santiago Bernabeu after a turbulent 2025/26 campaign.

Vinicius Jr had a very public falling out with coach Xabi Alonso before he was sacked in January, as Madrid ended without silverware for the second year on the trot.

“It was a very difficult season,” he said. “We started well, ahead of Barcelona, but then we began to lose and draw matches we should have won. We lost confidence and Barcelona gained momentum. It is the first time I have gone two seasons without winning. We failed. We have a team to win next year. Real Madrid always comes back.”

There have also been endless rumours around a lack of harmony in the dressing room, culminating in the fracas between Federico Valverde and Aurelien Tchouameni that left the former in hospital.

Vinicius Jr highlighted a lack of experience in the squad as one contributing factor.

“Without Nacho, without [Luka] Modric, with [Dani] Carvajal injured, without [Toni] Kroos, they gave a lot of experience to the team,” he said.

“Now Fede and I have experience on the pitch, but not in the locker room. We do not yet have enough experience to carry that burden. We still have to keep learning.

“This season we learned a lot about the locker room. Next season we will be a better group, more united, better as a team. We are going through a cycle where we have to change our roles to help.

“Sometimes it is good to see what you had and understand how hard it is to win everything we have won. I got used to winning. There is a lot of pressure. That is part of being at the best club in the world. People are waiting for us to fail, and we have failed two years in a row. We cannot fail again.”

articles.title: Lionel Messi likely to CONTINUE playing for Argentina after World Cup heartbreak
articles.summary: Lionel Messi is set to carry on playing for Argentina, according to reports in his homeland
articles.content:
Lionel Messi likely to CONTINUE playing for Argentina after World Cup heartbreak

Lionel Messi is set to carry on playing for Argentina, according to reports in his homeland

Last Update:

Argentina’s players returned home to a hero’s reception last night, although all the talk was around one man who was not there: Lionel Messi.

Messi remained in the United States following Sunday’s World Cup final defeat to Spain in New Jersey, and flew back to his home in Miami rather than joining his team-mates on the charter back to Buenos Aires.

The 39-year-old is expected to spend a few days in South Florida before travelling back to his home town of Rosario to see his father Jorge, who has been suffering from an undisclosed illness.

Messi has to decide whether to continue playing for Argentina after another remarkable World Cup in which he scored eight goals and added four assists in eight games to provide the inspiration for Argentina’s run to the final.

Reports in his homeland suggest Messi, who has scored 125 goals in 207 appearances, has played his last World Cup but is willing to play on until the 2028 Copa America, a tournament scheduled to be hosted by Ecuador but could yet be switched to the USA.

Argentina do not have to qualify for the 2030 World Cup as one of six co-hosts and CONMEBOL may implement a new format similar to the Nations League in Europe to determine which of the other teams advance.

Table of Contents

Messi – I hold on to all the good things

Messi’s disappointment at the defeat to Spain was evident at the time with tears pouring down his face. He took to Instagram last night to thank the Argentina fans for their support.

He wrote: “Thank you from the bottom of my heart for every greeting and message.

“The pain is immense and this wound will take time to heal. Once again, we managed to unite as a country and stand together, sharing the immense pride of being Argentine.

“It is hard to fully appreciate our achievement right now, but this group reached two consecutive World Cup finals.

“I also hold onto all the good things. The matches we turned around by giving it our all – moments that will remain in our memories forever – and the support of an entire country which, combined with this group’s hard work and effort, brought us back among the world’s elite once again.“I also want to congratulate Spain on winning the title.”

Messi could continue under new boss if Scaloni walks away

Messi’s future is thought to be unrelated to that of Argentina coach Lionel Scaloni, who hinted yesterday that he would leave the role when his contract expires in December.

He said: “I’ll be here until December, and then I’ll probably stop.

“Honestly, I feel the need to think because I don’t know if we’ll be able to do something as grand as this. We would need to talk. I am grateful to the president of the AFA for giving me this opportunity. To be in a place that I am in, which is a dream for everyone.

“We tried until the last minute to give it our all, the coaching staff and players. I think it’s just that I take the time to think.

“This place is marvellous. To continue, we need a lot of things. We need to reset. We need to form a group like this one, which is difficult to form again. It hurts my soul. I’m sorry.”

Scaloni was front and centre as the Argentina delegation landed home last night and was treated to an open-top bus parade from the airport with thousands of fans lining the streets to hail their efforts.

Argentina vs Spain: Lionel Messi stats

Messi became the second player in World Cup history to appear in three finals (2014, 2022 and 2026), along with Brazil’s Cafu (1994, 1998, 2002).

At 39 years and 25 days of age, he is the oldest outfield player to have appeared in a World Cup final, with Argentina the sixth reigning champions to have reached the decider.

Having won all seven of their preceding matches at the 2026 edition, Argentina failed to become the first team since Brazil, who won seven out of seven in 2002, to have a 100% winning record at a single World Cup.

When is Lionel Messi’s next match?

Messi’s club side Inter Miami resume their Major League Soccer campaign tomorrow night against the Chicago Fire but their talismanic captain will be afforded a lengthy break.

He is not expected to play in the next three MLS games and may also sit out the Leagues Cup clashes with San Luis, Monterrey and Club Leon.

articles.title: Kevin Keegan: England football legend dies aged 75 after cancer diagnosis as Newcastle, Man City, Liverpool, Fulham and Southampton lead tributes
articles.summary: Newcastle have called Kevin Keegan a 'true giant' in a tribute
articles.content:
Kevin Keegan: England football legend dies aged 75 after cancer diagnosis as Newcastle, Man City, Liverpool, Fulham and Southampton lead tributes

Newcastle have called Kevin Keegan a 'true giant' in a tribute

Last Update:

Newcastle have paid tribute to “remarkable” Kevin Keegan after the legendary former England forward and head coach, who won the Ballon d’Or in 1978 and 1979, died aged 75.

Keegan’s family announced in January that the three-time top-flight winner was set to begin treatment following a stage four cancer diagnosis.

“It is with immense sadness we announce that Kevin Keegan has passed away at the age of 75,” a statement from the family said on Monday.

“The former England player and manager had been battling cancer and was surrounded by his wife and daughters in his final moments.

“Kevin, a double Ballon D’or winner, was a much-loved husband, father and grandfather. The family would like to thank Kevin’s incredible medical team for all their support.

“This is a hugely difficult time and they are requesting space and privacy.”

A post shared by Newcastle United (@nufc)

Table of Contents

Kevin Keegan ‘inspired dreams’ – Newcastle

Seven years after ending his glittering playing career, Keegan assumed his first coaching role by becoming Newcastle manager in February 1992 and steering the Magpies to second-tier safety.

Keegan won promotion with the club the following season and, in the final season of his first spell in charge, guided Newcastle to a huge lead at the top of the 1996/97 Premier League before they were edged out by Manchester United in a classic title contest.

“Kevin was more than a legendary footballer and manager,” said a statement from the club.

“He was the beating heart of Newcastle United for generations of supporters. As a player [between 1982 and 1984], he brought world-class talent, ambition and belief to St. James’ Park, helping to transform perceptions of what Newcastle United could be.

“As a manager, he ignited our city. Kevin gave supporters hope and pride and led a team whose style, spirit and passion captured the imagination of football fans around the world.

“He was so much more than an entertainer. Above all that, Kevin forged an extraordinary bond with Newcastle, built on the roots of his father, Joe.

“He understood our people. He embraced the north-east with a passion that was genuine and unwavering and, in return, he earned his rightful place in the hearts of millions.”

Kevin Keegan career: Liverpool, Hamburg, Southampton, Newcastle, England

After starting his career at Scunthorpe United, Keegan joined Liverpool under iconic manager Bill Shankly in 1971.

As well as domestic glory, Keegan’s achievements at Anfield included winning the European Cup – now the Champions League – and the UEFA Cup, which is now the Europa League. Here’s the full list.

Keegan joined Hamburg in 1977, winning the Ballon d’Or in successive seasons with the German side, as well as the Bundesliga in 1979 and a run to the European Cup final in 1980.

Southampton signed Keegan in 1980 and he was the Player of the Season at the club in 1981/82, repeating that feat in both of his campaigns at Newcastle.

“Kevin signed for the club in 1980 as the holder of the Ballon d’Or and brought great joy to fans at [former stadium] The Dell and across the football world,” read a statement from Southampton, who said they were “devastated” by the news.

“Our thoughts are with his family and friends at this difficult time.”

Kevin Keegan international career

An England debutant in 1972, Keegan captained his country from 1976 until his retirement after the 1982 World Cup.

England also reached EURO 1980 with Keegan in attack but failed to make the knockout stage of either major tournament he featured in.

A back injury restricted Keegan to one World Cup appearance and he finished on 21 goals in 63 appearances, with only 18 players ever outscoring him for the national team.

Kevin Keegan: Newcastle, Fulham, England, Man City manager

Following that memorable first coaching spell at Newcastle, the man known as ‘King Kev’ joined Fulham in a senior role in 1997 and took over as manager before the Cottagers’ second-tier play-off campaign in 1997/98.

The club won promotion to the Premier League as champions in 1998/99. Keegan combined his role with taking charge of England from February 1999.

The charismatic figure left Fulham at the end of that season to concentrate fully on England, although the Three Lions failed to progress from their group at EURO 2000 despite a first win over Germany since 1966.

A World Cup qualifying defeat to Germany at Wembley Stadium in October 2000 caused Keegan’s immediate resignation, returning to football as Manchester City boss in 2001.

City adopted a cavalier style typical of Keegan on their way to becoming second-tier champions in 2001/02, and he managed them in the Premier League until his exit in March 2005.

To the delight of supporters, Newcastle re-appointed Keegan in January 2008. He left eight months later, with widespread reports of tensions with the club’s hierarchy.

“Kevin’s impact will not be measured by appearances or results,” added Newcastle’s statement following his passing.

“It will live on in the memories he created with club and country, the dreams he inspired wherever he went and the generations of supporters around the world who fell in love with football because of him.

“At this profoundly sad time, we send our love and deepest sympathy to Kevin’s wife Jean, his family, friends and all who had the privilege of knowing and working alongside him.

“We mourn the loss of a true giant of our history. At the appropriate moment, we will carefully consider how we shape a lasting tribute to Kevin’s remarkable life and legacy.”

Kevin Keegan tributes: England ‘incredibly saddened’

In a statement, England offered “thoughts and condolences” to Keegan’s family, friends and the football world, adding: “We are incredibly saddened by the news.”

One of Keegan’s finest players at club and international level, Alan Shearer, called him “my hero”.

“My manager,” said Shearer. “My friend. Sleep easy, boss.”

Former Liverpool and England defender Jamie Carragher described Keegan as “one of the greatest players this country has ever produced” and “an absolute giant of the English game”.

“One of the most important men in making Liverpool what it is today,” said Carragher.

Here are a selection of more of the tributes to Keegan from across football.

Liverpool: “We are deeply saddened by the passing of the legendary Kevin Keegan and mourn his loss.

“His indomitable spirit and remarkable contribution will be forever etched in our history and his legacy will live on. Rest in peace, Kevin.”

Manchester City: “Everyone at Manchester City is devastated to learn our former manager Kevin Keegan has passed away, aged 75.

“Kevin was a transformative manager who brought optimism and vibrancy to City during his four-year spell in charge.

“The promotion campaign in 2001/02 will never be forgotten, and Kevin then established us once again as a top Premier League side in the years that followed.

“Our thoughts are with Kevin’s family and friends at this very difficult time.”

Manchester United: “We are profoundly saddened by the loss of Kevin Keegan.

“A giant of English football, he was a cherished figure at the very highest levels of the game.

“Our condolences go to Kevin’s family, loved ones and all those he inspired as a manager, player and person, on and off the pitch. Rest in peace, Kevin.”

Fulham: “We’re incredibly sad to hear the news that our former manager, Kevin Keegan, has passed away.

“A legend of the game… our thoughts are with his friends and family at this difficult time.”

The EFL: “Saddened to learn of the passing of Kevin Keegan.

“A legend of the English game, Keegan will be remembered by generations of football fans for his impact as a player and manager. Our thoughts are with his family and friends.”

articles.title: Lamine Yamal trolls Argentina as Spain mock World Cup final fighting: ‘Event of the year’
articles.summary: Lamine Yamal and Spain partied after winning the World Cup 2026
articles.content:
Lamine Yamal trolls Argentina as Spain mock World Cup final fighting: ‘Event of the year’

Lamine Yamal and Spain partied after winning the World Cup 2026

Last Update:

Lamine Yamal jabbed a finger at a sign mocking Argentina’s Leandro Paredes as Spain celebrated their acrimonious World Cup final win in front of around two million fans in Madrid on Monday.

Joking atop a bus carrying Spain’s squad to a ceremony in the capital, Yamal and teammates including Fabian Ruiz laughed as they held up a sign calling Paredes’ shocking post-match altercation with Gavi the “event of the year”.

“VELADA DEL AÑO VII, PAREDES VS GAVI”.Lamine Yamal, pidiendo UNA PELEA DE BOXEO entre ambos jugadores, tras el cruce post Final del Mundo. 😳🇦🇷🇪🇸 pic.twitter.com/iBhbgBOYxw https://t.co/hW3Lz4d47A

The champions were in a suitably ecstatic mood as their made their way through the streets before the likes of head coach Luis de la Fuente and full-back Marc Cucurella sung on stage alongside musicians.

Barcelona’s Yamal has had an extraordinary eight days, having turned 19 last Monday, helped Spain beat France in the semi-finals last Tuesday and gone all the way at his first World Cup with the victory in New Jersey.

Table of Contents

Spain vs Argentina: What happened between Paredes and Gavi

Partly fuelled by Argentina midfielder Enzo Fernandez’s late second booking for a rash challenge, the game between the 2022 winners and the reigning European champions was frequently fractious.

Tempers flared in violent fashion after Spain’s extra-time win courtesy of Ferran Torres’ 106th-minute strike.

Boca Juniors midfielder Paredes pushed Spain counterpart Gavi to the ground in the most noticeable altercation as players from both sides attacked each other in an unedifying end to the most prestigious match in world football.

World Cup final 2026: Rodri praises Ferran Torres

Player of the tournament Rodri confessed he was lost for words at the ceremony, although the Manchester City midfielder led supporter chants for full-back Marc Cucurella, who played the drums at one point during the festivities.

“These lads here are amazing,” Rodri said, via AS. “I’d like to remember someone very important to me – a player who has been unfairly criticised and who today is a part of Spanish football history: Ferran.”

De la Fuente, who also led his team to the EURO title two years ago, thanked the nation.

“We are fortunate to have 26 fantastic people who are fantastic footballers,” added the 65-year-old. “The best in the world.

“It is an honour to manage them and share this moment with my coaching staff. Together, we are stronger – don’t forget that. Long live Spain.”

World Cup 2026: What Ferran Torres, Pedro Sanchez said

Barcelona’s Torres said he was “so happy” to see children enjoying the occasion. “We must always keep believing, because everything comes in time,” he told LA 1.

“I’m literally flying, because we’re back from New York. The goal… everything comes with hard work, and this time it has been like that.”

Spain’s prime minister, Pedro Sanchez, said La Roja could add to their two World Cup titles when they host the finals with Portugal and Morocco in 2030.

“I want to thank the [Spanish Football] Federation,” said Sanchez. “I know it’s a big effort for them to come and share this victory with everyone.

“A huge thank you to the coaching staff and the players for their performance, their effort and the win. We thoroughly enjoyed watching you play.

“Why not dream of a third in 2030? Especially with Spain as the host country.”

articles.title: Lionel Messi breaks silence on ‘immense pain’ of World Cup final result: ‘I want to congratulate Spain’
articles.summary: Lionel Messi has addressed Argentina's World Cup final defeat
articles.content:
Lionel Messi breaks silence on ‘immense pain’ of World Cup final result: ‘I want to congratulate Spain’

Lionel Messi has addressed Argentina's World Cup final defeat

Last Update:

Lionel Messi has used the parting words of his first message since the World Cup final to congratulate Spain after La Roja dethroned Argentina to leave the icon in tears.

Ferran Torres’ extra-time strike settled a tempestuous encounter, with Messi – who may have played the last match of his glittering international career – crying on the pitch before skipping interviews alongside his teammates.

“Thank you from the bottom of my heart for every greeting and message,” Messi wrote on Instagram.

“The pain is immense and this wound will take time to heal. Once again, we managed to unite as a country and stand together, sharing the immense pride of being Argentine.

“It is hard to fully appreciate our achievement right now, but this group reached two consecutive World Cup finals.”

A post shared by Leo Messi (@leomessi)

Table of Contents

Lionel Messi: How Argentina returned to ‘World Cup elite’

Messi had a sensational tournament, contributing eight goals and four assists in eight matches at the age of 39.

The icon led his country to the title in 2022 and was only outscored at the latest edition by 10-goal France striker Kylian Mbappe, who is the only player to have eclipsed Messi’s all-time total of 21 goals at the finals.

“I also hold onto all the good things,” reflected Messi, whose 125 goals and 207 caps are unsurpassed for Argentina.

“The matches we turned around by giving it our all – moments that will remain in our memories forever – and the support of an entire country which, combined with this group’s hard work and effort, brought us back among the world’s elite once again.“I also want to congratulate Spain on winning the title.”

Lionel Messi: No contact with Argentina boss Scaloni

Argentina head coach Lionel Scaloni joined Messi in being unable to hide his despair after the final whistle at the MetLife Stadium.

“I haven’t spoken with Leo,” Scaloni told Ole, suggesting that his tenure could end when his contract expires in December.

“As for me, I’ll talk to the president: I’ll fulfill my contract and then I’ll see. I feel the need to think. I don’t know if I’ll be able to do something as big as this [again].

“Maybe we’ll have to see. I thank the president for the opportunity, for giving me this position. This place is a dream for everyone.

“We tried until the very last moment to give our all as a coaching staff and players. It’s only fair that I can take this time and think about it.

“This place is wonderful – a dream place, one that my coaching staff and I never imagined we’d be in.

“To continue, a lot of things are needed: to reset, to form a group like this, which is unlikely to be formed again. It hurts me deeply. I’m sorry.”

Argentina vs Spain: Lionel Messi stats

Messi became the second player in World Cup history to appear in three finals (2014, 2022 and 2026), along with Brazil’s Cafu (1994, 1998, 2002).

At 39 years and 25 days of age, he is the oldest outfield player to have appeared in a World Cup final, with Argentina the sixth reigning champions to have reached the decider.

Having won all seven of their preceding matches at the 2026 edition, Argentina failed to become the first team since Brazil, who won seven out of seven in 2002, to have a 100% winning record at a single World Cup.

When is Lionel Messi’s next match?

While many members of Argentina’s squad have flown together to Buenos Aires, Messi has travelled to Rosario with his family.

His preparations could now begin for his return with MLS side Inter Miami, who have a packed schedule.

Assuming Messi takes a break for at least a week, here’s how the Herons’ fixture list looks for August. Asterisk denotes match starting on previous day in specified territory.

articles.title: UEFA boss boycotts World Cup final in protest against FIFA
articles.summary: UEFA president Aleksander Ceferin did not attend Sunday's World Cup final.
articles.content:
UEFA boss boycotts World Cup final in protest against FIFA

UEFA president Aleksander Ceferin did not attend Sunday's World Cup final.

Last Update:

UEFA president Aleksander Ceferin did not attend Sunday’s World Cup final between Argentina and Spain in protest against FIFA.

Although Ceferin travelled to Mexico City for the tournament’s opening match between co-hosts Mexico and South Africa, he opted not to attend the final in New Jersey following a series of disagreements with world football’s governing body.

One of the main reasons behind his decision was FIFA’s controversial move to overturn Folarin Balogun’s suspension after intervention from United States President Donald Trump.

UEFA strongly criticised the decision at the time, describing it as “unprecedented, incomprehensible and unjustifiable”.

“When the certainty of rules is no longer guaranteed by its guardians, the integrity of the game is at stake and the credibility of a competition is undermined,” UEFA said in a statement.

Ceferin is also opposed to several other initiatives introduced by FIFA president Gianni Infantino, including the introduction of half-time entertainment shows.

UEFA rejects half-time shows

The World Cup final featured performances from Madonna, BTS, Shakira and Justin Bieber, extending the traditional 15-minute interval to more than 27 minutes.

UEFA has no plans to introduce similar shows at the Champions League or European Championship.

The governing body also remains firmly against proposals to expand the World Cup to 64 teams, an idea Infantino suggested could be explored during the tournament.

Elsewhere, UEFA responded after Somali referee Omar Artan was denied entry to the United States before the World Cup by appointing him to officiate the UEFA Super Cup between Paris Saint-Germain and Aston Villa on August 12.

Ticket pricing has also been a point of disagreement. UEFA intends to broadly freeze prices for Euro 2028, allowing supporters to buy five match tickets for roughly the cost of a single parking space at a World Cup venue in the United States.

articles.title: Ibrahimovic retires from punditry after World Cup coverage
articles.summary: Football icon Zlatan Ibrahimovic has retired from punditry duties after the World Cup.
articles.content:
Ibrahimovic retires from punditry after World Cup coverage

Football icon Zlatan Ibrahimovic has retired from punditry duties after the World Cup.

Last Update:

Former Sweden striker Zlatan Ibrahimovic has announced he is stepping away from television punditry following the 2026 World Cup final.

The 44-year-old, who earned 122 caps for Sweden during his illustrious playing career, joined Fox Sports’ World Cup coverage this summer alongside Rebecca Lowe, Thierry Henry and Alexi Lalas for his first experience as a television analyst.

Following Spain’s 1-0 extra-time victory over Argentina in the World Cup final, Ibrahimovic revealed live on air that the tournament would mark the end of his broadcasting stint.

“I’ve been talking a lot for the last one-and-a-half months, so these will be my last words,” Ibrahimovic said.

“I want to thank America. I want to thank all the other people you don’t see. I don’t remember all their names, like Thierry does.

“I hope, America, you enjoyed it as much as I did. And this is also my farewell to the studio.”

When host Lowe asked whether he was leaving for good, Ibrahimovic confirmed there would be no return.

“This was the first and last time for me – so take care, everybody.”

Despite having no previous television punditry experience, Ibrahimovic quickly became a popular figure with viewers thanks to his outspoken analysis and trademark personality.

articles.title: Guardiola holds talks with Italy and considers swift return to football management
articles.summary: Paolo Maldini and Leonardo are reported to have spent the weekend in Barcelona in a bid to tempt Pep Guardiola back into football management
articles.content:
Guardiola holds talks with Italy and considers swift return to football management

Paolo Maldini and Leonardo are reported to have spent the weekend in Barcelona in a bid to tempt Pep Guardiola back into football management

Last Update:

Pep Guardiola has held talks over becoming the new head coach of Italy, according to reports in the country.

Sky Italia claim Italian FA (FIGC) technical director Paolo Maldini and advisor Leonardo spent the weekend in Barcelona trying to convince Guardiola to make a swift return to work after leaving Manchester City.

The Catalan left the Etihad at the end of last season after a trophy-laden 10 years in which he led the club to six Premier League crowns and the 2023 Champions League.

He vowed to take time off but is already pondering a return with the FIGC also considering Roberto Mancini, Antonio Conte and Andrea Pirlo as they look to appoint a successor to Gennaro Gattuso, who departed following Italy’s failure to reach this year’s World Cup.

The new president of the FIGC, Giovanni Malago hopes there will be an appointment in days.

He told told Sky Sport 24: “It took me two weeks to bring Paolo Maldini and Leonardo on board, because being serious people and with an interest in the project from the beginning, they wanted to go into the details of what I had in mind.

“With Maldini and Leonardo there is no confusion. On the contrary, we are talking about the details. A few more days of patience and you will know everything. Is the list limited to Mancini and Pirlo? There may be other possible names.”

Table of Contents

What has Guardiola said about his future?

Speaking last week, Guardiola insisted he was in no hurry to return to the dug out.

He told OKX: “People say ‘Ah – in three months you will be back, in six months you will be back’.

“Maybe, but I have to feel it and experience that I really miss it and need it. Right now, for these three weeks [or] a month, I [have woken] up in the morning and they said ‘oh, Pep – do you miss it?’

“I said ‘No. Okay, good. Let’s go’. That is what I feel right now. Maybe one day I will wake up and say ‘Okay, I want to be back – I want to prove again that I’m a good coach. I want to deal with the players and handle them, my sporting director and hierarchy.’ Right now, I don’t feel that.

“A lot of players – the young players, old players – they said ‘I want to leave. I’m here, in cold Manchester, I’m not playing. I want to leave.’

“And you have to replace those guys. But the big, big task is [about] the organisation, sporting director, manager, CEOs, the hierarchy, the recruitment of the right players that you need.

“Everyone makes mistakes with that. [It requires] making [less costly] mistakes [and making] as few as possible. That is the key point.”

Pep Guardiola: Football ‘life’ until Man City exit

A lack of “energy” and back problems contributed to Guardiola’s decision to “care for myself a little bit” by taking a break, he explained.

“[I want to] see much more of my kids,” he added. “My father is 95 and still here; my sisters, my brothers.

“[Going more] slowly is [partly] the target. And after [that], we will see. If I miss [football and] someone wants me to be back, [I’ll consider my options].

“Otherwise, I will continue. I’m not young anymore. I’m not 35, 36, 37, 40, 41. I always thought about why, during all my life, [everything is] always related to football.

“[Is all] I can do playing or managing football? Why don’t I try to discover a life or be happy or be complete as a human being doing other things, not just related to football?

“It’s a question mark. I don’t know, because since I was a little boy in my little town, [everything was] football, football, football until [I left City].

“Now I try to maybe enjoy doing other things that I’ve never done [and] now want to do.”

articles.title: World Cup 2026 Team of the Tournament: Messi headlines star-studded line-up
articles.summary: Discover who makes our World Cup 2026 Team of the Tournament.
articles.content:
World Cup 2026 Team of the Tournament: Messi headlines star-studded line-up

Discover who makes our World Cup 2026 Team of the Tournament.

Last Update:

The 2026 World Cup was everything the expanded format promised and several things nobody quite expected.

Spain arrived as European champions and left New Jersey as world champions, beating Argentina 1-0 in a scrappy final.

England reached their best World Cup finish since 1966, beating France 6-4 in a breathless third-place match in Miami.

Norway, at their first World Cup since 1998, reached the quarter-finals and knocked out Brazil in the process. Erling Haaland turned the tournament into his own private record book.

The United States, playing on home soil, went out to Belgium 4-1 with politics overshadowing the football, and Mauricio Pochettino’s tenure ended without the historic run the host nation had dreamed of.

Portugal were beaten by Spain in the last-16, and Germany were stunned by Paraguay. The chaos of a 48-team competition delivered exactly the kind of upsets and surprises its architects had promised.

Here is our team of the tournament, in a 4-2-3-1 formation.

Table of Contents

GK: Unai Simon (Spain)

The easy read on Spain’s tournament is that their goalkeeper had little to do.

In truth, Unai Simon was authoritative throughout, commanding his area with the quiet assurance of a goalkeeper completely at home on the biggest stage.

Spain conceded just one goal across the entire knockout phase, and the defensive organisation in front of Simon was as much a product of his direction from the back as it was of Cubarsi and Laporte’s excellence ahead of him.

In the final, when Emiliano Martinez was making saves that drew gasps, Simon barely had his gloves tested, but he still walked away with the Golden Glove.

RB: Pedro Porro (Spain)

Porro announced himself to a global audience at this tournament and left it as one of the best attacking right-backs in the world.

His goal in the 58th minute of the semi-final against France settled the tie and sent Spain to the final. He was equally impressive throughout the group stage and into the knockout rounds.

He ranked third in Spain’s internal FIFA Power Rankings for the tournament, behind only Rodri and Cubarsi, which tells you everything about his quality this summer.

CB: Pau Cubarsi (Spain)

Nineteen years old. Every minute of every game. Six clean sheets in seven matches. Those three facts alone would justify the inclusion, but the Cubarsi story at this tournament was about considerably more than the headline numbers.

He played 566 passes across Spain’s campaign, more than any other outfield player, completed more through balls than any other player at the tournament and was, according to Opta’s group-stage team of the tournament, the only player under 20 in their best XI alongside Messi, Mbappe, Haaland and Vinicius.

Against France in the semi-final, he held Mbappe scoreless. In the final, he was on the receiving end of the Enzo Fernandez challenge that produced Argentina’s red card and changed the match.

Cubarsi broke Sergio Ramos’s record as Spain’s youngest-ever defender, won an Olympic gold medal at 17, and has a €500 million release clause at Barcelona. He is 19. The sport has not produced a centre-back quite like him in a generation.

CB: Cristian Romero (Argentina)

The man who almost opted to skip Spurs’ relegation decider in May somehow became the defensive heartbeat of a run to the World Cup final two months later.

Romero arrived in North America carrying the baggage of a difficult club season, a torn MCL injury in April and questions about his commitment.

Against England in the semi-final, he was extraordinary. He could not prevent Torres’ winner in the final after leaving the pitch with a knock, but he gave everything in a campaign that reminded the sport of exactly how good he is at his best.

LB: Djed Spence (England)

Nobody on this list attracted more scepticism before the first ball was kicked. Spence’s inclusion in the England squad over Trent Alexander-Arnold was one of the most criticised selections of the summer, and the Spurs full-back arrived in North America carrying the full weight of that noise.

What followed was one of the great individual tournament redemption stories. He was used across both flanks by Thomas Tuchel, defensively elite whenever called upon, and produced the defining moment of England’s semi-final campaign against Argentina in a last-ditch tackle on Giuliano Simeone at a point when the tie was hanging by a thread.

His performances against Norway in the quarter-final and Mexico in the last-16 were crucial to England reaching the last four.

CM: Rodri (Spain)

Rodri was the quiet engine beneath everything Spain did at this tournament. In a squad full of technically gifted, eye-catching players, he was the one who controlled the pace, the tempo and the structure of every match Spain played.

His passing accuracy never dropped below 93% across seven games. He pressed without losing position, covered the ground behind Spain’s more adventurous midfielders and dictated when the team sped up and when they slowed down.

Against Argentina in the final, when Scaloni’s side tried to press high early in an attempt to disrupt Spain’s rhythm, Rodri simply bypassed the press and recycled the ball until the space opened.

He ranked first in Spain’s FIFA Power Rankings for the tournament. There is not a better defensive midfielder at a World Cup in recent memory.

CM: Jude Bellingham (England)

No midfielder has ever scored more goals at a single World Cup. Six goals across six matches, with an another goal in the third-place match against France to add to the tally, took Bellingham to seven direct contributions at a tournament where only three forwards, Messi, Mbappe and Haaland, scored more often.

He opened England’s tournament with the winner against Croatia, scored twice in 98 first-half seconds against Mexico in the last-16 to become the first player to score two goals in a match at Mexico City Stadium in a World Cup since Diego Maradona in 1986, then scored twice again against Norway in the quarter-final.

He won four Man of the Match awards. He became the youngest player in history to reach ten World Cup appearances, aged 23 years and six days.

CAM: Lionel Messi (Argentina)

Eight goals. Four assists. Twelve goal contributions, more than any other player at the tournament. His first World Cup hat-trick, scored against Algeria in the group stage opener after 31 appearances across five previous tournaments without one.

He broke Miroslav Klose’s all-time World Cup goals record against Austria to take his tally to 21. He scored or assisted in 11 consecutive World Cup matches. He has 10 knockout stage assists, six more than any other player in the recorded history of the competition.

Against England in the semi-final, with five minutes remaining and Argentina losing, he rolled the ball back for Fernandez’s equaliser and then crossed for Martinez to head home in stoppage time.

At 39 years old, in what was almost certainly his final match in a World Cup, against Spain in the final, he was held without a shot on target for the first time in the tournament. It did not diminish a single thing he did before it. He is the best player in the history of this competition.

RW: Ousmane Dembele (France)

Dembele arrived in North America as the reigning Ballon d’Or winner and had, across 19 consecutive major international tournament appearances before this summer, scored precisely zero goals.

He scored a hat-trick against Norway in the first 32 minutes of France’s final group game, the second-fastest hat-trick in World Cup history after Austria’s Erich Probst in 1954, the first by a Ballon d’Or winner since Cristiano Ronaldo against Spain in 2018 and the first first-half hat-trick at a men’s World Cup since Oleg Salenko in 1994.

He finished the tournament with seven goal contributions, adding further goals against Iraq and in the knockout stages.

LW: Kylian Mbappe (France)

France’s captain finished with 11 direct goal contributions, second only to Messi in the entire tournament, and was the central figure in the most explosive attacking team at the competition.

His assists for Dembele’s hat-trick against Norway were as impressive as any of the goals he scored himself.

He was electric against Senegal in the group stage, decisive against Morocco in the quarter-final and was the player Spain most feared going into the semi-final.

ST: Erling Haaland (Norway)

Seven goals in five matches. A conversion rate of 39 per cent from 18 shots. The best debut World Cup return since Grzegorz Lato’s seven goals for Poland in 1974.

He scored twice against Iraq on his first-ever World Cup appearance, once in the Round of 32 against Ivory Coast, twice in the dying minutes to knock five-time champions Brazil out of the tournament in the last-16.

Norway had scored five knockout stage goals in their entire World Cup history before this tournament.

He was the most physically intimidating forward at the competition, the most clinical in front of goal, and the single biggest reason a nation at the World Cup for the first time in 28 years reached the quarter-finals and had 80,000 people believing, right to the final whistle, that they could go further.

2026 World Cup Team Of The Tournament

articles.title: World Cup 2026: Five things we won’t miss
articles.summary:
There were some good things about the 2026 World Cup but a lot of bad.
Here, we outline the five things we won't miss.
articles.content:
World Cup 2026: Five things we won’t miss

There were some good things about the 2026 World Cup but a lot of bad.

Here, we outline the five things we won't miss.

Last Update:

The World Cup is done and dusted and consigned to the history books.

It was not a vintage tournament with few stand-out games and an elongated format that made it even harder for the leading nations to go out early on.

Here, we outline five things we won’t miss about the 2026 World Cup in the United States, Canada and Mexico.

Table of Contents

GIANNI INFANTINO

No doubt the man himself will describe having 48-competing teams as a huge success but, the truth is, it wasn’t. The group stage was low on jeopardy with the decision to rank teams level on points via the head-to-head method rather than goal difference another error.

Infantino was a visible presence throughout the tournament, often spotted networking with politicians, film stars and former players.

Questions remain about his suitability for the job but, unfortunately, there is no sign of him leaving his post. The expanded event merely strengthens his position – more teams means more revenue, and more support from confederations outside Europe.

The product may be worse but will someone think about the balance sheet…

SLACK REFEREEING

Most fans would rather the game be allowed to flow but FIFA’s relaxed approach went too far. It led to a lack of control from certain teams, culminating in Argentina’s thuggish approach to the final. Lionel Scaloni’s team played on the edge in the semis against England where a better referee would have clamped down on their tactics earlier, but it spilled over against Spain.

It will be interesting to see how referees tackle games when the major European leagues restart next month.

SLEEPING ON THE SOFA

There is no longer a need to stay up waiting for the 4am kick-off between Jordan and Algeria. Having a World Cup Stateside presents logistical problems that Europeans are not used to and it will be nice knowing that the big games that we are so accustomed to will be staged at more welcoming hours over the next 10 months.

DONALD TRUMP

Trump’s intervention that pushed FIFA into suspending the red card dished out to USA striker Folarin Balogun was a disturbing development. FIFA usually frowns on political interference but, here, usual protocol was disregarded to enable Balogun to play against Belgium.

It is worth noting that Balogun remained the only player to have any kind of card suspended during the whole tournament. FIFA has yet to explain its reasoning.

PROTEST INCONSISTENCIES

Palestinian flags were confiscated, as were those displaying the pre-revolutionary symbols of Iran. No politics? Fine. However, when Argentina’s players displayed a banner claiming the Falkland Islands were theirs, Andrew Giuliani, head of the White House FIFA task force, said it was fine due to the protection of free speech.

It was another mixed message to suit the US and its agenda.

articles.title: Belgium on the hunt for new coach after Garcia departs
articles.summary: Rudi Garcia has left his role as head coach of Belgium
articles.content:
Belgium on the hunt for new coach after Garcia departs

Rudi Garcia has left his role as head coach of Belgium

Last Update:

Belgium have parted ways with head coach Rudi Garcia.

The Red Devils reached the quarter-finals of the World Cup before losing to eventual winners Spain, but were largely unimpressive outside of the 4-1 hammering of the United States in the round of 16.

Garcia’s contract expires at the end of July and the two parties have mutually opted against an extension.

The 62-year-old said: “After discussions with the Royal Belgian Football Association (RBFA), we have decided not to extend the excellent journey we have shared over the past 18 months. I leave Belgium in League A of the Nations League and among the top eight teams in the world.

“I would like to thank my outstanding group of players, sports director Vincent Mannaert, and the fans who supported us throughout this World Cup. I wish Belgium every success as they continue the generational transition that I was proud to help initiate.”

Belgium chief hails Garcia for restoring team cohesion

Garcia took over from Domenico Tedesco in February 2025 and helped them avoid relegation to League B of the Nations League thanks to a 4-3 aggregate win over Ukraine in the play-offs.

Mannaert said: “Rudi Garcia has unquestionably played a key role in restoring the Belgian Red Devils. He was appointed national coach in a challenging sporting and financial context. Thanks in particular to his commitment and experience, team cohesion was restored and a strong result was achieved at the most recent World Cup.

“On behalf of the federation, I would like to warmly thank Rudi and his assistants for the past 18 months.

“Together with my team, I am currently preparing for a new cycle, including the appointment of a new national coach.”

Manchester United sign highly-rated winger Thompson from Tottenham

Manchester United have completed another piece of clever business this summer.

Last Update:

Manchester United have completed the signing of highly rated winger Tynan Thompson from Tottenham in a deal worth an initial £4 million, with a further £4 million payable in performance-related add-ons.

The 18-year-old joins Old Trafford after emerging as one of Tottenham’s brightest academy prospects and has been promised opportunities to challenge for a place in United’s first-team squad.

Thompson joined Spurs’ academy at the age of 12 and enjoyed an impressive campaign last season, scoring 13 goals and providing six assists across Under-18 and Under-21 level.

Seven of those goals came in seven UEFA Youth League appearances, while his performances also earned him two places on Tottenham’s Champions League matchday bench.

The agreement also includes a 15% sell-on clause in Tottenham’s favour, with the additional payments linked to Thompson’s achievements at first-team level for United.

Confirming the transfer, United said in a statement: “Manchester United have agreed the signing of exciting young winger Tynan Thompson, subject to registration. The England youth international has joined from Tottenham Hotspur.

“The 18-year-old scored 13 goals and contributed six assists last season across Under-18 and Under-21 level, including seven goals in seven UEFA Youth League games. His performances earned him opportunities within Spurs’ first-team matchday squads.

“Everyone at United would like to welcome Tynan to the club and wish him the very best of luck for the future.”

articles.content:
Aston Villa snap up Joao Gomes from Wolves as midfield overhaul continues

Aston Villa have announced the signing of Brazil international João Gomes from Wolves

Last Update:

Aston Villa have bolstered their midfield with the signing of Joao Gomes from Wolves.

Villa have paid an initial £34million for the Brazil international, who impressed at Molineux despite their relegation from the top flight last season.

Gomes made 130 appearances for the Black Country club, scoring seven times, after joining from boyhood club Flamengo in 2023.

He leaves Molineux with a glowing endorsement from the club’s technical director Matt Jackson.

Jackson told Wolves’ official website: “Joao deserves everything he gets from the game. He’s a model professional, a lovely young man and a great family man. He’s the type of professional that coaches love and players love, so he will go on to be the outstanding player that we know he is.

“We’re obviously sorry to see him go, but we have to take responsible decisions for the football club, and then we build to be stronger collectively. It’s a very natural part of football, the best run football clubs who don’t have unlimited resources have to work this way. The model is something that we have to adopt, and our fans have always been hugely understanding of that.”

Emery continues Villa rebuild

Gomes is part of a midfield overhaul at Villa Park with Morgan Rogers poised to join Chelsea in a £117m deal and Amadou Onana set to miss the bulk of next season having ruptured his ACL at the World Cup while playing for Belgium.

The 25-year-old Gomes will be joined at Villa by Switzerland international Johan Manzambi, who signed for Unai Emery’s men last week in a deal that could exceed £50m.

articles.title: Lionel Messi: Time to leave the international scene but remember the good times, not the shame of New Jersey
articles.summary: Lionel Messi could not conjure up one final piece of brilliance on a dismal afternoon for Argentina who ended the World Cup final in defeat and disgrace
articles.content:
Lionel Messi: Time to leave the international scene but remember the good times, not the shame of New Jersey

Lionel Messi could not conjure up one final piece of brilliance on a dismal afternoon for Argentina who ended the World Cup final in defeat and disgrace

Last Update:

Lionel Messi stood staring at the Argentina fans, tears streaming down his face.

Behind him, Spain were lifting the World Cup following a victory that was a triumph for quality, persistence and restraint.

The fact Messi and his team-mates did not turn round and watch the victors lift the trophy came as no surprise; it was merely a continuation of a classless attitude evident from the outset.

Their sole gameplan was to frustrate and cheat, using thuggish tactics in the hope it took them to a penalty shoot-out. Mercifully, for the game of football it did not succeed.

The antics of Leandro Paredes, who should have earlier joined Enzo Fernández in being sent-off, and Nahuel Molina at the final whistle, throwing punches at Spain players as they celebrated summed up a team that knew they had been handed a footballing lesson.

Argentina did not have a shot of any description until the 117th minute. That came from Messi on one of the few occasions he managed to escape the iron fist of Spain’s control.

Table of Contents

Messi’s final let-down after another brilliant World Cup

Messi, as always, had been Argentina’s star man throughout a tournament during which he turned 39 years of age. But he was a largely peripheral figure as Spain dominated the ball in a one-sided encounter. The Inter Miami star managed just 54 touches in 120 minutes and spent much of the afternoon trotting around as the European champions pinged the ball from one player to another.

As he did in Argentina’s successful 2022 campaign in Qatar, Messi dragged a collection of moderately talented players to the final with eight goals and providing the inspiration for many more.

But not even he could influence a fight as one-sided as this though and his obvious irritation spilled over in the second half of normal time as he attempted to get Marc Cucurella sent off for covering his mouth, waving his hand towards the sidelines like a child attempting to get the teacher’s attention. It was unbecoming of the eight-time Ballon d’Or winner and a desperate act of a man who knew his team were in need of help.

That it didn’t come was also a slight surprise. The widespread accusations that Argentina were given preferential treatment by referees may be misplaced but they were certainly on the right side of several key decisions throughout the tournament.

Slovenian official Slavko Vincic attempted to let the final flow but it was a nigh on impossible task due to Argentina’s persistent infractions with the only criticism being he ought to have clamped down on them earlier.

If he had then Messi and Co would undoubtedly have suffered a deserved defeat in 90 minutes, rather than having to wait until 106 for Ferran Torres to finally apply the killer touch.

Messi likely to walk away after fantastic international career

Given his age and the fact this appears the end of a cycle for Argentina with several ageing players, and coach Lionel Scaloni, set to walk away, it seems highly likely Messi’s international career is now over.

It is perhaps fitting it will end at the same MetLife Stadium where he announced his international retirement in 2016 after a Copa America final defeat to Chile, their fourth final defeat in nine years.

Having been persuaded to carry on, Messi returned with a bang, perhaps not initially as a disjointed side failed to make much of an impression in Russia in 2018, but his moment was to come three years later with victory at the Copa America.

Argentina backed that up by lifting the trophy in Qatar – their first world crown in 36 years – before another Copa win in 2024.

Messi was the driving force behind them all and it is only right to focus on those successes rather than dwell on the angry, bitter, miserable performance against Spain.

Only Messi knows what the tears represented at the final whistle. Disappointment, regret, perhaps even a little embarrassment at being caught up in Argentina’s shameful approach in New Jersey.

In the end, it doesn’t really matter. Messi will now disappear once and for all from the biggest stage and spend his final months, or years, torturing defences in Major League Soccer.

Thank you for the memories, it’s just a shame it had to end this way.

articles.title: Argentina boss Lionel Scaloni likely to leave in December following World Cup heartbreak
articles.summary: Argentina's World Cup-winning boss Lionel Scaloni says he will most likely walk away in December when his contract expires
articles.content:
Argentina boss Lionel Scaloni likely to leave in December following World Cup heartbreak

Argentina's World Cup-winning boss Lionel Scaloni says he will most likely walk away in December when his contract expires

Last Update:

Argentina coach Lionel Scaloni has confirmed he will probably leave the post when his contract expires in December.

Scaloni took over in 2018 and has enjoyed a golden period in charge, leading his country to two Copas America and the World Cup title in 2022. However, the team’s attempts to win a second world crown ended in disappointment and disgrace in New Jersey last night with a dreadful performance against Spain – they didn’t register a shot until the 27th minute of extra-time – as the European champions won 1-0.

Argentina’s gameplan was to frustrate and they used all the dark arts to achieve it with Enzo Fernandez sent off in the second half of normal time. Their frustration spilled over after the final whistle when Leandro Paredes and Nahuel Molina started brawling with Spain players as they celebrated.

Despite bizarrely claiming his players know how to lose gracefully, Scaloni deserves huge credit for enabling a fairly limited side to reach the final once again.

He broke down in tears at the official post-match press conference when discussing his future and confirmed in the mixed zone that he was set to depart at the end of the year.

I’ll probably stop, says Argentina boss Scaloni

He said: “I’ll be here until December, and then I’ll probably stop.

“Honestly, I feel the need to think because I don’t know if we’ll be able to do something as grand as this. We would need to talk. I am grateful to the president of AFA for giving me this opportunity. To be in a place that I am in, which is a dream for everyone. We tried until the last minute to give it our all, the coaching staff and players. I think it’s just that I take the time to think.

“This place is marvellous. To continue, we need a lot of things. We need to reset. We need to form a group like this one, which is difficult to form again. It hurts my soul. I’m sorry.”

It is likely to be a period of change for Argentina with several ageing players coming towards the end of their international careers, most notably Lionel Messi.

articles.title: ‘We know how to lose’ – Scaloni humble in defeat as Argentina fail to defend World Cup title
articles.summary: Argentina boss Lionel Scaloni says his side know how to lose after heartbreak in the World Cup final.
articles.content:
‘We know how to lose’ – Scaloni humble in defeat as Argentina fail to defend World Cup title

Argentina boss Lionel Scaloni says his side know how to lose after heartbreak in the World Cup final.

Last Update:

Lionel Scaloni paid tribute to his players and accepted Spain were worthy winners after Argentina’s bid to defend the World Cup title ended in a 1-0 defeat after extra time at MetLife Stadium in New Jersey.

Ferran Torres scored the only goal of the final in the 106th minute, converting from close range after Nico Williams’ cross had found Mikel Merino at the back post.

Argentina had survived 90 minutes thanks to an extraordinary display from Emiliano Martinez, who made 11 saves to break the World Cup final record and keep Spain at bay.

Argentina did not register a single shot in normal time, the first team in history to achieve that unwanted distinction in a World Cup final, but they resisted to the very end before Enzo Fernandez’s second yellow card in the 90th minute reduced them to ten men and ultimately opened the door for Torres to settle it.

Scaloni, who has managed Argentina since 2018 and overseen a golden era that delivered the 2021 Copa America, the 2022 World Cup and the 2024 Copa America, was gracious in defeat.

“I feel sad but I am aware that we played our hearts out. There are many things I would like to say, but I can’t really. I am forever thankful to these guys who have competed all the way,” he said.

“They were better to be honest. I have really fond memories of what they did and how difficult it is to get here.

“We need to attach a great deal of value to what we have done. We are big in victory and we must be big in defeat. Today we showed that we know how to lose.

“We lost the game and we accept that. But it doesn’t mean that we will forget everything we have done so far. I would like to tell the country that we played our hearts out.”

Messi’s farewell

The defeat almost certainly marks the end of Lionel Messi’s World Cup career.

The 39-year-old, playing his sixth and final tournament, was kept quiet throughout the final by a Spain side that afforded him almost nothing.

He finished without a shot on target, a stark contrast to a tournament in which he had broken Miroslav Klose’s all-time World Cup scoring record and become the first player in history to score or assist in 11 consecutive World Cup matches.

Spain’s combination of Pau Cubarsi and Aymeric Laporte at centre-back, sitting behind a world-class midfield, denied Messi the pockets of space that had defined his tournament up to that point.

He gave the ball away more than any other Argentina player on the night, a first in a 2026 campaign that had produced moments of brilliance that will outlast the result.

articles.summary: Spain boss Luis de la Fuente could not hide his emotions after his side won the World Cup.
articles.content:
De la Fuente hails ‘example’ Spain after World Cup win: ‘I can’t really tell you how I feel’

Spain boss Luis de la Fuente could not hide his emotions after his side won the World Cup.

Last Update:

Luis de la Fuente was lost for words and swimming in pride after Spain were crowned world champions for the second time in their history, beating Argentina 1-0 after extra time at MetLife Stadium in New Jersey to complete the greatest double in the sport.

Ferran Torres settled one of the finest World Cup finals in recent memory with a close-range finish in the 106th minute, arriving to convert after Nico Williams had pulled a cross back into the box.

It was a goal that ended a contest Argentina had somehow kept goalless for 90 minutes through the extraordinary brilliance of goalkeeper Emiliano Martinez, who made 11 saves to break the World Cup final record and single-handedly keep the defending champions alive long after Spain’s domination had suggested the result was inevitable.

Argentina’s resistance finally crumbled deep into stoppage time when Enzo Fernandez was shown a second yellow card for a foul on Pau Cubarsi, reducing Lionel Scaloni’s side to ten men for extra time.

From that moment, Spain’s eventual victory felt only a matter of when rather than if. Torres provided the answer 37 seconds into the second period of extra time.

The result means Spain have now won the European Championship and the World Cup in successive summers under De la Fuente, who took the job in 2022 with, as he put it in his semi-final press conference, “an idea, a philosophy” that has taken the nation to the summit of world football.

Speaking after the final whistle, the Spain manager could barely contain his emotion.

“So much pride. Pride for this generation of footballers that have been growing with this idea, staying loyal to the idea, and doing their best,” he said.

“They are an example of a team, a group, a family, and a collective of great players that have been exceptional. I’m just so proud to have accompanied them on this journey, to have been there with them on this trajectory is an honour.

“I can’t really tell you how I feel. All I can say was it was worth it. Of course at the moment I am very emotional, particularly having watched from behind the scenes.

“I have spoken so much to the players, who said to me, ‘Boss, we’ve won it all’, and it’s marvellous. This generation of players is an example for Spanish sport, for the Spanish youth. Together we are much stronger, and that is why we don’t forget anyone.”

‘We like to suffer’

De la Fuente acknowledged that even with that level of dominance and with Argentina reduced to ten men, the night had demanded everything Spain had.

“Of course we would have liked to win the game much sooner. The Martinez save prevented us from doing so.

“We tried and tried to get on the scoresheet but weren’t able to, but this is a World Cup final, even against ten men at the end we had to suffer. But, we like to suffer, and I’ll say it again, we were prepared for everything.”

The lowdown on the World Cup 2026 final and half-time show

Last Update:

Spain, Argentina and a gaggle of pop stars will attempt to make the 104th and final match of the World Cup 2026 a spectacle to remember on Sunday.

Eight-time Ballon d’Or winner Lionel Messi is hoping to inspire the holders and finish as the tournament top scorer.

La Roja’s ranks include 19-year-old sensation Lamine Yamal and former Ballon d’Or winner Rodri, with the performers on the pitch set for an extended half-time break while music takes centre stage in New Jersey.

Justin Bieber will co-headline alongside Madonna, Shakira and K-pop (or Korean pop) boy band BTS in a ceremony FIFA say will combine “football, music and social impact”.

What time is the World Cup final 2026?

The match kicks off at 20:00 BST on Sunday, July 19. Here’s how that translates in different territories.

Where is the World Cup final 2026?

The game will take place at the MetLife Stadium in New Jersey, which has a capacity of almost 81,000.

The spectacular setting is the home of NFL teams the New York Giants and the New York Jets and will host its eighth match at the finals, averaging more than three goals per game.

Contests held at the venue have included record five-time champions Brazil’s group-stage draw with Morocco and quarter-final defeat to Norway.

France beat Sweden and Senegal at the MetLife Stadium, which was the stage for Ecuador’s surprise win over four-time champions Germany during the group phase.

What time is the halftime show at the World Cup 2026?

Assuming there are no weather delays, the half-time show should start shortly after the end of the first half. Here are the earliest times it could start.

World Cup 2026 halftime show: Who is playing?

Pop megastar Shakira is partly responsible for the official World Cup 2026 song, Dai Dai, and will be joined by colossally popular Nigerian singer Burna Boy, her collaborator on the record.

This is the first time a half-time show has taken place during a World Cup final and the ceremony has been arranged by English band and familiar American stadium fillers Coldplay.

BTS will be back at the MetLife Stadium in August for two dates as part of their US tour. “They’ll be part of a moment that reaches far beyond the pitch,” half-time show producers Global Citizen promised of the performance.
